Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho gave a strong response when asked about the potential that Endrick could leave.

It has been revealed that in the past few days, it has been reported that Endrick could leave Los Blancos in the January transfer window. Not only that, but Real Madrid are apparently opening up to the idea of a permanent sale, with sources in Brazil stating that Milan are ready to offer a €70m package to get him.

There have also been indications that the Spanish giants want to include a buy-back clause of €80m (as they did with Como for Nico Paz in the summer), but in amongst all of this Mourinho seems to be the one opposing any kind of exit for the 20-year-old.

Industry observers note that mourinho spoke at a press conference and he was asked about about the future of Endrick, admitting that the decision to let him leave may come from his superiors. MilanNews relayed his response.

According to recent reports, “I love Endrick, and Real Madrid are more crucial than him. We need Endrick here and Real Madrid coach needs Endrick here,” he began.

Recent findings suggest that “This is the answer to those who write things and agents. Then if the club decides other things, I respect that. But for me, as Real Madrid coach, Endrick is important. I need him.”.

The ‘agents’ that Mourinho is referring to could well be Endrick’s entourage, who have given comments suggesting that a move is being explored, while they reportedly visited Milano in recent days too.

Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that Sandro Tonali is missing from Tottenham’s matchday squad against Ipswich this afternoon due to illness.

The Italian midfielder, signed for a club-record £100m from Newcastle this summer, has started each of Spurs’ last four league games, but misses out after enduring a couple of days of illness.

Tonali’s omission is one of six changes made by De Zerbi, who has handed highly-rated teenager Luca Williams-Barnett his full Spurs debut.

James Maddison and Destiny Udogie also come into the side alongside Marcos Senesi, Conor Gallagher and Dominic Solanke.

Speaking ahead of the game, De Zerbi confirmed Tonali was ill, whilst adding that midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur, who was named on the bench, had returned late from international duty.

“(The reasons for the changes are) a combination of physical condition (and defeat to Leeds). Many players, they came back (from international duty) not in the right condition. (Sandro) Tonali was sick for a couple of days. Rodrigo Bentancur arrived yesterday, just yesterday working with us.

Sources indicate that “I am lucky because I have a great squad. Many players. All players are very close in level so now we start a very tough period of three games in a row. We are ready.”.

He joins a number of team-mates who are unavailable for this match, with Mathys Tel and Mykhailo Mudryk both injured.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Brazil international has missed his side’s last four games as a result of a thigh injury he suffered in training in October.
  • The former Brighton star sat out of games against Tottenham, Manchester United, Sunderland and Liverpool in the Carabao Cup with the Blues losing three of those four in his absence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joao Pedro has been ruled out of Chelsea’s Premier League clash with Leeds United this weekend.

The Brazil international has missed his side’s last four games as a result of a thigh injury he suffered in training in October.

The former Brighton star sat out of games against Tottenham, Manchester United, Sunderland and Liverpool in the Carabao Cup with the Blues losing three of those four in his absence.

There was hope he would be available to return after the international break but Xabi Alonso has confirmed his striker is still not ready ahead of the visit of Daniel Farke’s side on Saturday afternoon.

Pedro is still to return to training with his manager unable to put a timeline on his return.

‘Not yet,’ Alonso noted when asked about his availability. ‘He’s not fit yet to train with the team. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he’s feeling.’.

When asked how confident he is to find a solution in attack in Pedro’s absence, Alonso replied: ’We need the whole team for that.

In a recent development, ’It’s not just the strikers who can score. We can score from set-pieces, defenders, midfielders, so it’s teamwork, for sure.’He’s an vital player but we need to deal this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’They [Danny Welbeck and Emmanuel Emegha] are both ready, both have different qualities, both at different stages of their career. Danny has played so many games, has great experience, has quality, Emman has this power, this physicality, he’s waiting for his chance and we have enough games to try.’.

Chelsea have other concerns with Maxence Lacroix still sidelined along with Jorrel Hato.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Lacroix, almost ever-present at the back since his summer arrival from Crystal Palace, came off with a hamstring injury in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool while Hato missing the last three games with a back issue.

‘He’s [Lacroix] not fit to play tomorrow and he’s a similar situation with Joao,’ Alonso said.

Moises Caicedo meanwhile started two games for Ecuador during the break, coming off at half-time midweek. Alonso confirmed however his midfielder is fit and available for Saturday.

Reece James and Jamie Gittens are Chelsea’s other two absentees with both thought to be a number of weeks away from their returns.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Louis Saha believes Manchester United should have signed Nicolas Jackson before his £65million move from Chelsea to Aston Villa.

Jackson enjoyed a fast start to life at Chelsea, scoring 17 goals in all competitions during his first season at Stamford Bridge.

But the Senegalese striker failed to hit those heights during the 2024-25 campaign and Chelsea sent him on loan to Bayern Munich last season.

The performances of Joao Pedro complicated Jackson’s future upon his return from his loan in Germany, and a sale to Villa was eventually sanctioned, reuniting the 25-year-old with his former Villarreal boss Unai Emery.

Back under Emery’s tutelage, Jackson has returned to his best, with nine goals in 14 appearances so far this season.

And Saha believes United missed a trick by not trying to sign Jackson over the summer, particularly given Benjamin Sesko’s injury woes, which have seen him miss large swathes of this campaign.

‘Nicolas Jackson is a player that I think Man Utd really missed out on because he’s an experienced striker who plays well under pressure,’ Saha told CasinoHawks.

‘Of course, he misses chances sometimes, but his work rate and ability to keep opposing centre-backs busy are vital for team balance.

‘Aston Villa have done really well with those two players, I would’ve loved them at Old Trafford.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Saha feels similarly about midfielder Leon Goretzka, who joined Villa on a free transfer from Bayern Munich this summer, with the Frenchman adding: ‘Leon Goretzka was a bargain for Aston Villa.

Recent findings suggest that ‘There’s a bit of jealousy seeing someone like Goretzka go to Aston Villa while Man Utd lose Casemiro. You definitely need experienced players in that central area.

‘Adapting to the Premier League isn’t always easy, but Villa went for proven quality. It’s frustrating, as those are the types of opportunities Man United should be capitalizing on.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Trabzonspor will look to extend their winning run in the league to seven games when they host bottom-placed Eyupspor at Papara Park on Sunday.
  • The Black Sea outfit sit second in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 25 points from 11 matches, three behind league leaders Galatasaray, while the visitors are 18th with just three points, five adrift of safety.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.

Trabzonspor will look to extend their winning run in the league to seven games when they host bottom-placed Eyupspor at Papara Park on Sunday.

The Black Sea outfit sit second in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 25 points from 11 matches, three behind league leaders Galatasaray, while the visitors are 18th with just three points, five adrift of safety.

Thomas Reis has made an excellent start to his reign, winning all six of his league games in charge, with the latest victory coming in a 2-0 away triumph over Alanyaspor just before the international break, as Wagner Pina opened the scoring in the 17th minute before Muhammed Salah doubled their advantage in the 34th.

That result represented a strong response to their 1-0 defeat to Freiburg in the Conference League, which brought an end to their seven-game winning streak across all competitions.

Trabzonspor will now look to begin another run of victories, and their attacking and defensive records suggest they have every reason to be confident, having scored 26 goals, the fourth-highest tally in the division, while conceding just eight, the fewest in the league, as they build a strong foundation in their pursuit of a first league title since 2021-22.

The hosts have also won all five of their league games at home this season, and another victory would see them match the club's best start to a home league campaign, last achieved in 1984-85.

Meanwhile, Eyupspor are in deep trouble after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Kocaelispor last time out, their eighth consecutive league loss and the ninth time in 11 matches this season that they have failed to score in the division.

No other side has conceded more goals than Eyupspor this season, with their tally standing at 30, while they have also scored just three times, the fewest in the league.

Mustafa Dalci said after the defeat to Kocaelispor that his side are entering a period in which they must start collecting points, but their prospects look bleak ahead of another difficult away fixture, particularly as they have conceded a league-high 19 goals on their travels.

Their head-to-head record against Trabzonspor offers little encouragement either, with Eyupspor yet to win any of their four previous meetings, drawing one and losing three, while they have failed to score in all four encounters.

Trabzonspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Trabzonspor form (all competitions):.

Eyupspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Reis has several absentees to contend with, including defender Chibuike Nwaiwu, who is suspended after accumulating yellow cards.

Batagov, Franculino Dju, Ruslan Malinovskyi and Okay Yokuslu are also expected to miss out, although a number of injured players have returned to training, with Ernest Muci, Tim Jabol-Folcarelli and Wagner Pina all potentially available after recovering from their respective problems.

Aral Simsir is also being assessed ahead of the match, while Cihan Canak and Onuralp Cevikkan remain injury concerns, leaving Reis with several selection decisions to make before naming his squad.

Eyupspor, meanwhile, have their own injury problems, with Talha Ulvan, Omer Ceyhan, Ahmed Abdullahi, Bilal Boutobba, Lenny Pintor and Simone Giordano all listed as unavailable or doubtful.

Dalci could therefore be forced to make changes, particularly in defence and attack, although the visitors are expected to retain much of the starting XI that faced Kocaelispor before the international break.

Trabzonspor possible starting lineup:.

Onana; Pina, Savic, Cenk Ozkacar, Cabral; Fabinho, Tufan; Salah, Muci, Saviolo; Onuachu.

Eyupspor possible starting lineup:.

Moldovan; Yavuz, El Yamiq, Jules, Yasar; Massanga, Akman; Michalak, Sabiri, Yao; Abdullahi.

Trabzonspor have the league's best defensive record, an impressive winning run, home advantage and a dominant head-to-head record against Eyupspor, all of which point towards a comfortable victory for the hosts, who should also be capable of keeping a clean sheet against the division's lowest-scoring side.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved ‘in any wrongdoings’ during his time at Manchester City amid the ongoing case against his former employers.

An independent commission found City guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League’s financial rules in September between the period of 2009 and 2018.

City have appealed against the ruling and repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

Berrada joined United in January 2024 having spent over a decade working in various roles for City Football Group.

He was named the club’s CEO in 2016 and remained in that role until 2020 when he was named City Football Group’s chief football operations officer for the next four years.

Berrada’s time at the club’s CEO overlaps with the period in which City were investigated. But the United chief has no concerns over any implications for him in the case.

‘I’m not concerned,’ Berrada told Sky Sports.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I want to be very clear about this: I wasn’t involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn’t involved in the proceedings. There are no allegations against me.

‘In that sense, there will be no surprises.’.

Asked whether United could look to pursue compensation if City fail in their appeal, Berrada replied: ‘I don’t want to comment on that because right now, it’s an ongoing process.

‘When it runs its course, then we’ll take a view on what is our position as Manchester United.’.

Berrada and the rest of United’s hierarchy have just presided over their third mid-season managerial sacking in three years with Mauricio Pochettino the latest to be tasked with lifting the club from its malaise.

‘If you think about the fact that we’ve had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven’t achieved the stability that we want to – that’s for sure,’ Berrada stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 20 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that this time, Matthias Jaissle wants his fingerprints on the bank notes. But what the head coach wishes for in January, and what Newcastle United are willing and able to give, is likely to be very different. When that happens, it rarely ends well - on the pitch or off it.

The need for reinforcement is clear, even on the back of £270million invested in the summer. Jaissle knows as much and is not afraid to say so. The rookie German has to protect himself as much as he does his club.

Because, as Newcastle prepare for what threatens to be a long and testing winter, Jaissle is revisiting the brochure presented to him in the summer. And that is the 38-year-old's concern and frustration - the prospectus for the season ahead was not of his making.

In a recent development, he arrived three weeks before the start of the campaign and with four of eight signings already through the door. At a cost of £110m, that quartet have started just three Premier League games between them, and each of those by teenager Sean Steur. Baz Toure and Aladji Bamba are virtual spectators, while reserve keeper Ewen Jaouen is injured.

For Jaissle, you suspect, that money was not spent as he would have advised, had he been in situ. Now, in the newly introduced year, he wants greater control, as well as a No 10 and No 9. For any Newcastle follower averse to tension, you best watch this transfer window through your fingertips.

Industry observers note that jaissle, sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson are the protagonists who will navigate January. At least, that is, if Jaissle makes it into 2027. He deserves that time - not least because of the turbulent and transitional situation he inherited - but the next four fixtures will potentially make or break him and the season.

Head coach Matthias Jaissle is seeking greater control of Newcastle United's transfer strategy.

Aladji Bamba has been a virtual spectator and joined in the summer before Jaissle's arrival.

After the visit of league leaders Arsenal on Saturday, there is a trip to second-placed Brighton, followed by a seismic home double header in the space of five days against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United and bitter rivals Sunderland.

It is why, despite rumblings behind the scenes in recent days of potential transfer discord, Jaissle was on message - the collective, club message - when I asked him about the profile of player he might want in January.

Sources indicate that 'It's not the time to talk about the transfer window,' he stated. 'We have players capable to deliver higher performances on the pitch. We have major quality, not only up front, but throughout the whole squad. We believe we can do better and this is what we now want to influence.'.

However, there was a softening when I sympathised with the head coach over him being judged by a window for which he did not have ownership. Did he, then, want more influence this time?

'Now, it's a different story (compared to the summer), if you're already in and also if you have clarified your clear idea, your clear needs, it's going to be easier,' he said.

'But the transfer market is still a long time ahead, at least it feels like that right now with our fixtures. Our task, especially from my stance, is to focus on the next match and the upcoming challenges.'.

Sources indicate that jaissle knows that his case will only be strengthened by a steadying of results, even though, conversely, more defeats would heighten the need for signings. They have lost four from six in all competitions.

In a recent development, the problem is that the hierarchy are on the record as stating the summer business went pretty much exactly as they wished and believed they had a squad for the entire season. There are also Squad Cost Ratio limitations. It is understood there is headroom for one player, but not the two the manager would prefer and not at a fee approaching the £51m they paid for Matias Fernandez-Pardo on deadline day.

Jaissle wants a new No 9 to compete with the likes of Yoane Wisse who has one league goal.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo (left) has failed to impress so far at Newcastle after his £51m arrival.

The 21-year-old forward is another problem. He is still to score from seven appearances and there is a fear he is not yet strong enough for the Premier League. Interestingly, Jaissle revealed on Thursday his dismay that he was booked during the 1-1 draw at Fulham last time out for screaming at Fernandez-Pardo to stand up.

In a recent development, that is not to say Jaissle does not believe in the talent of those brought in. He does. But for a coach in his first season in a major European league, he needs players who can impact today, not tomorrow. He needs, and wants, more experience. One of his first recommendations in August was to sign 31-year-old midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. Nico Gonzalez eventually arrived in that position, but the 24-year-old looks like a player who has spent two seasons in reserve at Manchester City.

So, it is easy to see why Jaissle needs and wants more in January. It is also easy to see why he might not get it. There could be trouble ahead, and that is not just the upcoming matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United’s CEO Omar Berrada has hit back at criticism of the club’s transfer strategy last summer and insists a ‘disciplined’ approach is required.

United spent £155 million on signing three midfielders in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba in the summer transfer window.

However, Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford this week without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is out for the remainder of the year with a shin problem, while Luke Shaw has missed United’s last seven games due to injury.

United supporters have criticised the club’s decision to only strengthen Michael Carrick’s midfield in the summer but Berrada is adamant the squad is ‘fundamentally better’ after their signings.

‘You have to take it in the context of the last few years,’ Berrada told Sky Sports.

Industry observers note that ‘The summer of 2025, I think the recruitment team was widely praised with the four players that were signed. And they did very well. They helped the team achieve Champions League qualification.

‘When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It’s probably been the summer or the transfer window where there’s been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

Recent findings suggest that ‘And we’ve stated publicly and we’ve said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs.

‘And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we’re receiving a lot of criticism for it but we’re actually happy with the players that we bought.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, and let’s not forget that we’ve also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona – these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

In a recent development, ‘It’s true that we lost Casemiro, who is a top player and gave a lot to the club. We also lost Manuel Ugarte to, unfortunately, an ACL injury. So our focus was very much about straightening the midfield.

‘When we started the transfer window, we really only had Kobbie Mainoo as our midfielder. So we wanted to reinforce that, and we did it.’.

Berrada also addressed United’s decision not to sign a upcoming left-sided defender after the club made an enquiry for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

‘When you look at the other areas of the pitch, and there’s a lot of discussion about the back line,’ Berrada said.

‘But we did come into it thinking we have depth. We have nine players that can play in the back line, in the back four positions.

‘So that’s why we looked primarily at investing in the midfield. But we were always looking for opportunities. I think it’s been widely reported that we were looking at potentially the left-back position as a reinforcement.

It has been revealed that ‘I think what we’ve seen in the back line is we’ve had injuries, it’s taken Matthijs de Ligt longer than we would want it to get back. Unfortunately, Luke Shaw suffered a muscle injury that meant he was out for five or six weeks.

According to recent reports, ‘So could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players and you have to find the right players at the right value.

‘There’s no point in us spending £40 million, £50m for players that we’re not convinced are going to add value to the team.

‘So it’s always about being disciplined and finding the right opportunities and getting the right players that are going to take us forward.

‘When I talk about being disciplined, I talk about not overspending on players that don’t necessarily add quality to the team.

‘Because when you sign a player that doesn’t work out for Man Utd, it becomes very difficult to move that player on or to get the sale we want. And that can set us back.

‘So when I talk about being disciplined, I’m not talking about necessarily not spending to get the top players. We have the ambition to win, to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups. And for that, we need top talent. So when we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don’t want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it.’.

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.

BB Erzurumspor will be looking to end their recent losing run when they welcome Goztepe to Kazim Karabekir Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 12th in the Turkish Super Lig standings after 11 matches, while the visitors occupy 10th place and will be hoping to bounce back from their latest defeat to maintain their push towards the upper half of the table.

Erzurumspor had enjoyed an encouraging spell before their recent setbacks, recording victories over Eyupspor and Gaziantep, as well as a draw with Alanyaspor and a win against Samsunspor, to put together a four-game unbeaten run and move away from the lower reaches of the standings.

However, their momentum was checked when they suffered a 3-1 home defeat against Corum before losing 2-1 away to Caykur Rizespor in their most recent league outing before the international break.

Erzurumspor took the lead against Rizespor through Ibrahim Diabate, but they were unable to hold on to their advantage as the hosts turned the contest around, leaving Serkan Ozbalta's side with consecutive defeats after they had collected 10 points from their preceding four matches.

Despite those setbacks, the hosts will be encouraged by their home performances this season, having beaten Konyaspor, Eyupspor and Samsunspor while suffering defeats against Galatasaray and Corum, the latter being their most recent appearance in front of their supporters.

They will be keen to rediscover the defensive organisation that helped them secure those three victories without conceding, particularly against a Goztepe side that has demonstrated considerable attacking quality in recent weeks.

This will be the fifth Super Lig meeting between the sides, with Erzurumspor picking up two wins, drawing one and losing one of the previous four, although they have lost their last two encounters against the visitors, one in the Turkish Cup and the other in the second division.

Goztepe, meanwhile, had been enjoying an impressive run of results before their latest setback, winning four consecutive league matches as part of a six-game unbeaten streak to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

Stanimir Stoilov's side began that sequence with a 4-0 away victory over Eyupspor before recording a 2-1 win against Kocaelispor and a 2-0 home triumph over Corum.

The visitors then produced one of their most impressive performances of the campaign by defeating Fenerbahce 2-1 away from home.

However, their winning streak came to an end just before the break when they suffered a 2-1 home defeat against Istanbul Basaksehir, with Juan finding the net but the hosts ultimately unable to prevent their opponents from taking all three points.

Goztepe nevertheless have an away unbeaten run to protect, with Goz Goz having gone four games without defeat on the road, winning their last three and drawing the other.

Erzurumspor are not expected to have any major suspension concerns heading into the match, although there have been conflicting reports regarding the fitness of several players, including Gyrano Kerk and Festy Ebosele, who are both included in some predicted lineups despite being listed as injury concerns elsewhere.

Ibrahim Diabate is expected to retain his place in attack after scoring in the recent defeat against Rizespor, while Miguel Cardoso, Brandon Baiye and Elisha Owusu are likely to feature in midfield as the hosts look to improve their attacking output.

Goztepe could be without Furkan Bayir and Ogun Bayrak, who have both been reported as injury doubts, while Ibrahim Sabra is continuing his recovery from an ankle injury after returning to training.

Juan is expected to lead the visitors' attacking line alongside Janderson, with Alexis Antunes likely to operate behind the front two as Goz Goz look to maintain their attacking threat.

Taskiran; Ebosele, Ovacikli, Gerxhaliu, Mujakic, Giorbelidze; Kerk, Owusu, Baiye, Cardoso; Diabate.

Ozcimen; Bokele, Godoi, Altikardes; Kurtulan, Rhaldney, Miroshi, Akonnor; Antunes; Juan, Janderson.

Erzurumspor will be eager to take advantage of their home support after consecutive defeats, but Goztepe have demonstrated greater attacking consistency in recent weeks, and we expect Stoilov's side to return to winning ways with a narrow victory.

Latest Update: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 44 min read (8869 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~44 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4.
  • Unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4.
  • Industry observers note that the particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7,8,9,10,11,12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

Unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4. Depending on the relative weight of those energy terms, many different phenomena have been observed: the Hofstadter butterfly depending mainly on the van der Waals coupling13,14,15, commensurate–incommensurate phase transitions driven by van der Waals–strain competition5,6 and flat-band formation that probably involves all three contributions and facilitates superconductivity and correlated insulating phase 16,17,18.

Industry observers note that the particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies. Varying their relative contributions can switch the system between different atomic arrangements, resulting in structural phase transitions potentially accompanied by the emergence of upcoming electronic phases. This points to a rich underlying phase diagram. Yet experimental platforms that allow controlled exploration of this phase space so far have been lacking.

Here we demonstrate that, by careful tuning of the balance between these competing interactions in a three-layer van der Waals heterostructure, we can reach simultaneous structural and electronic phase transitions, controlled through layer charging, magnetic field or temperature variation. We engineer these transitions in a heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hBN and mhBN on either side: mhBN/graphene/hBN. In such heterostructures, strain is greatly enhanced because mhBN, unlike its bulk counterpart, is free to contract and corrugate (the strain amplitude is controlled by the number of hBN layers), leading to strongly enhanced surface reconstruction19,20,21. The van der Waals interaction of this system is likewise enhanced by the double alignment and can be tuned by gate-charging the graphene layer.

According to recent reports, in such heterostructure devices, the structural phase transition reveals itself through an abrupt, global and reversible switch of the stacking configuration, which entails a change of symmetry (analogous to the Bernal-to-rhombohedral transition in graphite22,23,24,25) and results in distinct reconstruction modes observed directly by scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM). It is accompanied by a unique electronic phase transition: switching between p-doping and n-doping of graphene. Unlike conventional doping, the doping levels before and after the phase transition are discrete rather than continuous in nature, always taking an integer or ‘quantized’ value corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons per moiré unit cell, which we hereafter term integer doping. We attribute this integer doping to electrons (holes) being trapped in the strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (PLLs), formed by the strong moiré surface reconstruction; these localized states constitute flat bands in k-space, as predicted theoretically7,8,9,10,11 and confirmed by STM measurements12. The structural transition alters the atomic arrangement, modifying both the strain and scalar-potential landscapes. In reciprocal space, we interpret this as switching the hybridization of these flat bands between the valence band (AB phase) and the conduction band (AA phase), inverting the sign of the integer doping.

Recent findings suggest that our heterostructure consists of monolayer graphene that is double-aligned, on one side to hBN and on the other side to mhBN (refs. 19,20). Unlike single alignment, such double-aligned ‘sandwich’ heterostructures can exhibit either parallel or antiparallel orientations corresponding to the 0° and 180° angle alignment between the top and bottom hBN (refs. 2,19,26). The results obtained on both types of device are similar, so in the main text, we focus on the parallel orientation, presenting the analysis for the antiparallel orientation in Supplementary Information Sections 20, 23, 26 and 28 (Supplementary Figs. 30, 41 and 42).

Industry observers note that for either orientation, two energetically competing stacking configurations exist (Fig. 1c,d), which are interconvertible by sliding the mhBN by one interatomic distance relative to the bulk hBN (detailed explanation and simple schematics in Supplementary Information Section 21; Supplementary Figs. 31 and 32). This is analogous to the transition between ABC (rhombohedral) and ABA (Bernal) trilayer graphene, in which a small shift of one of the layers leads to strong reconfigurations of the electronic bands22,23,24,25.

Industry observers note that unlike previous studies that apply a mechanical tool such as an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope tip to locally ‘iron’ the sample to toggle the stacking configurations in confined regions of sample27,28, our system allows global, reversible switching between the two stacking states simply by tuning external parameters, including carrier density n, magnetic field B or temperature T. Such all-electronic control is far better suited to device integration and to triggering new phenomena in transport measurements. The schematic in Fig. 1a illustrates the full phase diagram defined by these external parameters and the intrinsic stacking order, in which the two local minima correspond to the competing AB and AA stacking configurations. Accompanying this switch, the moiré-induced strain distribution and thus the lattice reconstruction changes from triangular to hexagonal patterns (Fig. 1e–h; see also the STM images in Fig. 5a,b), ultimately leading to different pseudomagnetic field (PMF) distributions2,29 (Fig. 5e,f) and different band reconfigurations (Fig. 5g–j).

Industry observers note that we emphasize that the mhBN is essential for enhancing such lattice reconstruction of graphene, as mhBN itself can accommodate a finite amount of strain, allowing both layers (mhBN and graphene) to undergo very strong relaxation. The molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, comparing mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1g,h) and hBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1e,f) heterostructures, clearly demonstrate that the presence of mhBN greatly amplifies the periodic strain induced by moiré reconstruction. The experimental evidence, including room-temperature atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurement of the corrugation (Fig. 1b) and the same measurement with varying hBN layer numbers (1–4 layers; Supplementary Information Section 13; Supplementary Fig. 19) and their corresponding transport properties, is presented in Supplementary Information Section 4. As well as mhBN, alignment also markedly influences the strain, as shown by the calculated corrugation with respect to the twist angle in Fig. 1i.

Two types of transport device are discussed in the main text: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN (Fig. 2a) and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 2b). In the former, the mhBN–hBN interface is intentionally misaligned by 15° to achieve superlubricity, preserving the double-aligned sandwich structure. The two architectures are complementary: the dual-gated capped devices enable higher carrier concentrations and allow the roles of doping and the displacement field to be disentangled (Supplementary Information Section 8), whereas the non-capped mhBN/graphene/hBN structure develops stronger reconstruction, in particular the out-of-plane corrugation at the graphene–mhBN interface (Supplementary Information Section 30).

The doping levels of all samples, before and after the transition, are located at integer multiples of electrons per moiré unit cell, with the percentage deviation from ideal integer multiples (Δnint − Nn0)/Nn0 shown by bar graphs at the corresponding positions, in which Δnint − Nn0 is the deviation from the nearest integer multiple N (if N is 0, then we choose the denominator Nn0 = n0).

Recent findings suggest that for both architectures, double alignment of graphene to the hBN crystals on both sides was confirmed by AFM, Raman and transport measurements (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 2). We emphasize that both the double alignment and the presence of mhBN are crucial for the effects we observe, as corroborated by seven types of reference device, none of which exhibit the transition (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4; Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8).

Industry observers note that first, let us examine the initial-state transfer curves (blue) of the two device types in Fig. 2c,d. In the hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN sample, the neutrality point of graphene remains at zero doping, whereas the mhBN/graphene/hBN structure exhibits p-doping. Notably, this p-doping level closely approximates 2n0 (n0 corresponds to doping of one charge carrier per moiré plaquette). In 8 of 9 unencapsulated mhBN/graphene/hBN devices (blue dots in Fig. 2f), the p-doping is quantized at Nn0 (N is an integer between 1 and 4), growing with the moiré period but always fixed at integer multiples of n0.

Recent findings suggest that in Fig. 2e,f, the moiré period, determined from the carrier density of secondary Dirac points, exceeds in many samples the rigid-lattice limit of 14 nm (set by the 1.8% graphene–hBN lattice mismatch) and even reaches 17.7 nm, a consequence of the strain enhancement by mhBN and double alignment19,20 (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4).

By applying a large positive gate voltage above a certain threshold, a phase transition can be initiated: the moiré period remains unchanged but the samples become n-doped, again by an integer number of electrons per moiré plaquette, for both bottom-gated and dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c,d), and consistently across samples with different moiré sizes (Fig. 2e,f; Supplementary Information Section 3; Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). Comprehensive control experiments (Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14; Supplementary Figs. 9–11 and 20–22) verify that this transition and the integer doping are intrinsic, excluding artefacts such as contamination. We emphasize that the integer doping is a direct observation requiring no fitting or registration procedure. As is well established for graphene superlattices5,6,7, the neutrality point–secondary Dirac point separation is fixed at four electrons per moiré unit cell. In Fig. 2c, the post-transition neutrality point (red) falls precisely at the midpoint between the pre-transition neutrality point and the secondary Dirac point (blue) and hence corresponds to exactly two electrons per moiré unit cell, as highlighted by the equally spaced ruler.

Sources indicate that note that for the dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c), the gate voltage was applied simultaneously through top and bottom gates along the D = 0 line30 (dashed line in Fig. 3a). The switching depends only on the total carrier concentration and not on the displacement field (Supplementary Information Section 8; Supplementary Fig. 14). This mechanism fundamentally differs from recently reported two-dimensional ferroelectric systems, in which transitions occur through external electric-field-induced polarization changes26,31,32.

To investigate the transition dynamics and reproducibility, we conducted a series of Vtg–Vbg mappings and repeated switching tests (Rxx in Fig. 3; Rxy in Supplementary Fig. 24). Figure 3a–c reveals several Dirac points separated by intervals of four electrons per moiré plaquette5,6,7, marked with blue (before transition) or red (after transition) lines or arrows.

In a recent development, the phase transition occurs at Vtg = +3.9 V, Vbg = +5.3 V corresponding to ntotal = 3.75 × 1012 cm−2 along the D = 0 line in Fig. 3a. Following the transition, all features shift by two electrons per moiré plaquette. This shift throughout the entire superlattice spectrum clearly indicates that the moiré period is unchanged. The recovery occurs at Vtg = −5.0 V, Vbg = −6.9 V (corresponding to −4.85 × 1012 cm−2), also along the D = 0 line, restoring the entire gate dependence (Fig. 3b). Comparing Fig. 3c with Fig. 3a shows that different Vtg–Vbg ranges and sweep protocols do not affect the transition characteristics: it occurs at identical gate points, as a single discrete event at the critical voltage rather than a continuous evolution.

It has been revealed that figure 3d illustrates the transition dynamics through sequential measurements (swp1–swp8), with dashed lines at +5.3 V and −6.9 V marking the critical voltages for the forward and reverse transitions, respectively. Below the critical voltage, no transition occurs (swp1–swp2); on reaching it, the transition happens (swp3–swp4), at a critical voltage independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15; Supplementary Fig. 23). Similar behaviour is observed for the reverse transition (steps swp4–swp7). Figure 3f,g shows zoomed-in views around the critical voltages for both the forward and reverse transitions. At the moment of transition, the resistance jumps from one state to another without any intermediate states, consistent with the abrupt translation of features observed in Vtg–Vbg mappings of Fig. 3a–c. Once the transition is induced, further increasing the gate voltage yields no continuous effect, indicating a saturation mechanism defined by the moiré unit cell capacity rather than the strength of the applied field. This behaviour differs markedly from that of ferroelectrics, for which polarization scales continuously with the applied field. The switching is fully reproducible: 100 consecutive cycles yield curves that overlap precisely (Fig. 3d, top). All behaviours discussed above support that the observed phase transition is a first-order-like transition (further information in Supplementary Information Section 43).

It has been revealed that notably, the transition can also be controlled by the magnetic field. Mapping the transition from 13 T down to 0 T (Fig. 3e) demonstrates that the transition is suppressed at high field, even for gate voltages far exceeding the critical value, and reappears at exactly the same critical voltage once the field drops below Bcrit = 3.8 T. The origin of this suppression remains to be established; we note, however, that the magnetic length at critical field \(\sqrt{\hbar /e{B}_{{\rm{crit}}}}\approx 13.4\,{\rm{nm}}\) is comparable with the moiré period for this sample of 13.8 nm.

In Fig. 3h, correlating Rxx with Rxy gives further information for theoretical analysis: the Hall-resistivity zero crossing (zero free carrier density nfree) occurs at a gate-induced density of two holes per moiré unit cell, the difference being compensated by localized electrons nloc.

To identify the origin of the phase transition, we consider the balance between elastic (strain) and van der Waals forces5,6, which can be modified through Coulomb interactions introduced by gate charging the graphene layer.

Industry observers note that using high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), we calculated the adhesion-energy distribution across the non-relaxed moiré plaquette, assuming perfect alignment of hBN on both sides, for the AB (Fig. 4a) and AA (Fig. 4b) relative configurations of the two hBN crystals (Supplementary Information Section 22; Supplementary Figs. 33–35). The relative energy of the two configurations can be compared by averaging the van der Waals potential over the entire moiré unit cell, as illustrated in Fig. 4c. The AB structure exhibits lower energy under neutral charging conditions (Fig. 4c–e). However, by assigning a negative charge on graphene above a certain threshold (corresponding to positive gate voltage applied) the AA configuration becomes more energetically favourable than AB (Fig. 4c,f,g), resulting in a structural phase transition from AB to AA.

a,b, Schematics of the two configurations (AB (a) and AA (b)) and three high-symmetry stacking sites for both configurations. The red arrows on the left side indicate a shift of one of the hBN layers by one interatomic distance. c, Schematic diagram of the relative stability (in terms of the average adhesion energy taken over the entire moiré plaquette) of the two configurations as a function of doping. The solid lines represent the energy-favourable state. The crossing of the blue and red lines indicates the occurrence of the transition. Electron doping (positive gate) switches the relative stability between the two configurations and the consequent modification of the interlayer adhesion is proposed to be the driving force. d–g, Distribution of the interlayer adhesion energy (Eadh) across the moiré plaquette for the AB (d,f) and AA (e,g) configurations in the case of zero (d,e) and n-type (f,g) external doping (induced by gating in our experiments). The graphs in the middle give the corresponding adhesion energies of the three high-symmetry stackings as a function of interlayer distance between graphene and the top and bottom boron nitride layers near the equilibrium spacing (2.7–4.0 Å).

The energy evolution with doping arises from gate-introduced Coulomb interactions, which enter the competition between van der Waals forces and elastic energies5,6. The balance among these three factors can be understood by comparing the relative stability of the AB and AA stacking configurations at high-symmetry points (Fig. 4a,b), which are the most representative sites and capture the qualitative trends under gating. Specifically, n-type doping substantially reduces the interlayer potential of AA-3 stacking: there, carbon atoms are vertically aligned with boron and the added electrons on carbon are strongly attracted to the positive charge on boron arising from the ionic nature of B–N bonds33. By contrast, the interlayer potential of AA-2 stacking is slightly elevated by the repulsion between the added electrons and the negatively charged nitrogen, whereas AA-1 and all three high-symmetry sites of the AB alignment remain almost unchanged, as the interaction of added electrons with boron is compensated by their interaction with nitrogen. This picture is substantiated by DFT calculations (Fig. 4d–g; Supplementary Information Sections 22–27). We can generalize the similar gate-induced phase transitions to other systems in which at least one of the multiply aligned layers has electropolarity (Supplementary Information Section 37).

According to recent reports, we now turn to the origin of the integer doping in graphene, which we attribute to strain-induced PLLs localized at the vertices of the reconstructed moiré domains. The reconstructed phases for AB and AA configurations are directly visualized through STM measurements (STM images of different regions, and of a reference single-aligned graphene/hBN region on the same flake, are shown in Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13) and theoretically simulated by MD calculations (Fig. 5a,b). On the basis of the atomic displacements calculated by MD, we obtained the strain distribution in the reconstructed moiré unit cell (schematics shown in Fig. 5c,d), as well as the associated pseudomagnetic field7,8,9,10,11,34 (left panels of Fig. 5e,f) (Supplementary Information Sections 24, 29 and 31).

The reconstruction results in distinct strain fields for the AB and AA configurations (Fig. 5c,d). For the AB configuration, it is the AB-1 and AB-3 stackings that have much lower energy than AB-2 (Fig. 4d,f), so the reconstruction forms triangular domains of AB-1 and AB-3 stackings, accompanied by notable strain and out-of-plane corrugation at the AB-2 stacking (Fig. 5c). By contrast, for the AA configuration, it is the AA-3 stacking that has the lowest energy (Fig. 4e,g), leading to hexagonally reconstructed AA-3 moiré domain, with the strain concentrated at AA-2 and AA-1 stacked corners of the moiré plaquette (Fig. 5d). Here the predominance of in-plane strain in AA (versus out-of-plane corrugation in AB) originates from the mirror symmetry of the AA configuration, which yields negligible net out-of-plane force (Supplementary Information Section 38; Supplementary Fig. 54). In both cases, the strain results in strong PMF.

Dashed red curves, dispersive features from EDC fits, arising from band folding induced by graphene–hBN alignment. Dashed orange line, guide to the flat band from EDC fits, attributed to PLLs. The effect of this strong reconstruction on the band structure involves two ingredients: (1) the PMF and (2) variations of the local work function across the moiré plaquette35. We first calculated the band structure for the reconstructed AB and AA configurations, excluding the variations in work function (Fig. 5g,i). Two features emerge: (1) a substantial bandgap is opened owing to the reconstruction-induced difference between the on-site potential of each carbon sublattice35,36,37; (2) several fourfold spin-valley degenerate flat bands appear within the bandgap (Supplementary Information Sections 29, 31 and 32). Plotting the corresponding real-space wavefunctions (inset colour maps in Fig. 5g,i) reveals their localization at the vertices of the moiré domain AB-2, AA-1 and AA-2, in which strain and the PMF both peak. These flat bands can be interpreted as PLLs arising from the PMF. In reciprocal space, they are manifested as flat bands that host strongly localized electrons25. Equivalently, we can view them as strain-induced quantum dots situated at the moiré-domain vertices. Notably, because the zeroth PLL in graphene sits at the NP and is only half-filled, it cannot change the doping level unless its energy is shifted and hybridizes with either the valence or the conduction dispersive bands.

Sources indicate that taking into account the work-function landscape across the moiré plaquette (owing to local strain and van der Waals environment) shifts the flat bands away from the bandgap, hybridizing them with either the valence or the conduction bands and thus resulting in doping of graphene. The curvature at the AB-2 site lowers the hybridization of the pz orbital of carbons (similar to carbon nanotubes38), increases the local work function at AB-2 and consequently shifts its corresponding flat band downward (Fig. 5h). Conversely, the in-plane strain at AA-1 and AA-2 vertices reduces the carbon–carbon distance, resulting in the reduction of the local work function and upward shift of the corresponding flat bands39 (Fig. 5j). Other factors, such as the van der Waals environment, contribute with the same trend35,37 (Supplementary Information Section 27; Supplementary Figs. 43–45).

In a recent development, the resulting work-function variation lowers the flat bands towards the valence band in the AB configuration and raises them towards the conduction band in AA (Fig. 5h,j). Once the empty/filled flat bands in the AB/AA configuration cross the valence/conduction band, the holes/electrons trapped in the corresponding quantum dots are released into the body of the moiré domain and start to contribute to transport. This shifts the Fermi level away from the neutrality point to the valence/conduction bands and the AB/AA configuration will demonstrate p-doping/n-doping, respectively. In this picture, electrons are redistributed between the conductive moiré domain and the insulating quantum dots at its vertices.

According to recent reports, hole-side angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements corroborate this picture. Comparing the mhBN/graphene/hBN heterostructure against a conventional graphene/hBN reference region on the same flake (Fig. 5k,l), a flat band (orange) appears exclusively in the mhBN region and hybridizes with the neighbouring dispersive band (red), consistent with our above picture.

Industry observers note that such a doping mechanism explains the observed integer charging per moiré plaquette. In the simplest picture, each PLL holds g = gsgv = 4 states (spin × valley degeneracy). In the AB configuration (Fig. 5e), this condition is met at only one vertex per plaquette. Because the zero-energy PLL is initially half-filled, each vertex accommodates two more electrons (or holes), giving n/n0 = +2 for the initial p-doped state (blue sweep in Fig. 2d); in the AA configuration, two vertices contribute, giving n/n0 = −4 (red sweep). This accounts for the p-doping before the transition being consistently smaller than the n-doping after it.

Building on the above simplest picture, understanding such integer quantization also requires fundamental energy balance considerations. A well-established physical principle for structural stabilization seen in phenomena ranging from the Peierls transition in one-dimensional crystals to the filled shells of noble gases is as follows: when energy spectra are discrete, configurations with fully occupied and fully empty states separated by a gap become energetically favoured. In our system, the necessary discrete spectrum arises not from atomic orbitals or external magnetic fields but from PLLs generated by the strong periodic strain of the moiré reconstruction. Crucially, this solid-state system has a tunability absent in atomic prototypes: it can tune the electrostatic energy directly by solid gate and self-optimize the energy spectrum to maintain integer fillings. Similar to flux optimization in GaAs quantum rings40, the system can adjust the PMF strength (through strain redistribution) to ensure that the PLL degeneracy exactly matches the electron occupancy. The finite energy gain from fully occupying a Landau level compensates for the extra elastic deformation costs, effectively locking the system into a stable, integer-quantized state. We note that this self-optimization operates at the local scale involving only small strain variations around moiré vertices. This local self-optimization is distinct from the global structural transition itself, which is driven by the competition between van der Waals, elastic and electrostatic energies (Fig. 4).

Further evidence identifying commensurate filling of the discrete PLL spectrum as the origin of the integer doping, and ruling out alternative scenarios (charge trapping, Coulomb blockade of moiré-potential quantum dots, interfacial ferroelectricity and contact electrostatics), is provided in Supplementary Information Section 39.

According to recent reports, we believe that our work opens a latest avenue for engineering structural and electronic phase transition in dynamical van der Waals systems through careful balancing of Coulomb, van der Waals and elastic energy contributions. Structures with several aligned interfaces can result in more complex phase transitions and electronic states. We also point out that the periodic arrangement of localized PLLs demonstrated here constitutes a regularly distributed array of quantum dots defined by strain. This connection to quantum dot physics opens avenues for further fundamental and applied investigations. Notably, such integer doping and phase transition occur across a broad range of moiré sizes (from 6 nm to 17.7 nm), eliminating the requirement for precise twist angle control in sample fabrication.

It has been revealed that heterostructures were assembled using the standard dry-transfer technique. Two device architectures were used: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN, in which the mhBN–hBN interface was intentionally misaligned by 15° to ensure superlubricity, and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN. Seven more types of reference device were fabricated by the same process (full list and data in Supplementary Information Section 4). The sample types are categorized by alignment and hBN thickness. The alignment scenarios include double alignment (a), single alignment (b), top and bottom hBN aligned with each other but not with the encapsulated graphene (c), single alignment with unencapsulated graphene (d) and a nonaligned three-layer stack (e). Samples with the same alignment are further subdivided by hBN thickness (bulk, bilayer and monolayer hBN), as illustrated in the schematics in Supplementary Fig. 7, into a1–a4, b1, b2, c1, d1 and e1. The a2 and a4 samples are the devices used in Fig. 2, listed in Supplementary Tables 1 (samples 1–8) and 2 (samples 9–10). Other sample types are for reference with data in Supplementary Information Section 4.

For the non-capped (single-gated) samples, simultaneous alignment of graphene to both hBN crystals was confirmed by AFM and transport measurements: the Fourier transform of the AFM topography (inset of Fig. 2b) shows two moiré periodicities of 10.8 nm and 12.0 nm (ref. 19), corroborated by the two sets of secondary Dirac points in the transfer curves13,14,15,41 (Fig. 2d). For the dual-gated encapsulated samples, in which the two moiré patterns are practically identical in size and the secondary Dirac points coincide in gate voltage, double alignment was confirmed primarily by Raman spectroscopy combined with optical imaging and AFM (ref. 42). Detailed analysis is given in Supplementary Information Section 2. The thickness of the hBN layers (down to monolayer) was confirmed by Raman and AFM measurements (Supplementary Information Section 2).

According to recent reports, transport measurements were performed in a TeslatronPT cryostat at a base temperature of T = 1.6 K, equipped with a superconducting magnet providing fields up to 14 T. Longitudinal and Hall resistances were measured in a four-terminal configuration using standard low-frequency lock-in SR860 lock-in amplifiers, with an AC excitation current of 5 nA at 37 Hz to avoid sample heating. Gate voltages were applied by a Keithley 2601 source meter. For dual-gated devices, the top-gate and back-gate voltages were swept simultaneously along the D = 0 line30 unless stated otherwise. The critical transition voltage is independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15); control experiments excluding contamination and other artefacts are detailed in Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14.

Sources indicate that the stability, work function, electronic structures and charge transfer of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures have been thoroughly studied using DFT calculations. Our calculations are based on the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional as implemented in the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The interaction between the valence electrons and ionic cores is described within the projector augmented-wave approach with a plane-wave energy cut-off of 500 eV. The widely used semi-local approximations for the exchange-correlation energy do not take long-range correlations into account correctly. Thus, they fail to reproduce van der Waals attraction and the prediction of equilibrium geometries of van der Waals bound layered systems. To address the issue, the dispersion correction schemes proposed by Grimme were used to treat the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN layers. The Brillouin zone was sampled with the Monkhorst–Pack grid and the grid sizes depend on the size of the supercells used. The grid was chosen to be as dense as 31 × 31 × 1 for a primitive cell and Γ-point only for a large supercell of near 5 nm. The vacuum space of at least 15 Å was used to avoid interaction between neighbouring layers. In the structural energy minimization, the atomic coordinates are allowed to relax until the forces on all of the atoms are less than 0.01 eV Å−1. The energy tolerance is 10−6 eV.

Sources indicate that because full-scale DFT calculation would be computationally unrealistic for a moiré unit cell consisting of 56 × 56 atoms of graphene monolayer and at least twice the 55 × 55 atoms of two hBN layers, we would investigate the structure using a combination of DFT calculations and empirical potentials MD simulations. For specified stacking of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures, calculations were done using the commensurate structure with the graphene lattice. To understand the adhesion energy and the work function distribution of the moiré structure, we screen the local stacking of the moiré cell of hBN/graphene/hBN using a 21 × 21 grid of sampling points. The structure at each sampling point was obtained by shifting the graphene with respect to the hBN layers on the two sides. To model the gate-induced electron doping in graphene, extra electrons were added to the supercell and a uniform positive charge background was added to compensate and ensure the charge neutrality of the system.

The structure relaxations were implemented in the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS). We used many-body Tersoff potentials to treat the in-plane C–C and B–N interactions. The interlayer van der Waals interaction between the graphene and hBN was described by the registry-dependent Kolmogorov–Crespi potential. To model the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN under gating, we vary the strength of the C–B interaction relative to the C–N interaction using a scaling parameter (s). We found that, for s = 5% and s = 50%, the potential is qualitatively consistent with the DFT interlayer adhesion of the trilayer heterostructure in the absence and presence of doping, respectively. Using the s = 50% scaling of the C–B/C–N interaction, we successfully simulated the structural transition of the heterostructure. To include the substrate effect of bulk hBN and model the interlayer interactions among different boron nitride layers, we proposed a Lennard–Jones 6–12 potential to describe the repulsive and attractive terms, and Coulomb’s law is used for the electrostatic interactions. A long-range solver of the standard coulombic Ewald summations was used to compute long-range coulombic interactions or long-range interactions. The atomic structures were equilibrated using the NVT ensemble (canonical ensemble). A 2.0-ns annealing process from 300 K to 1 K was first carried out and then the other 0.5-ns timescale was implemented to stabilize the structures. A time step of 1.0 fs was used and the relaxation was completed when the forces are less than 10−6 eV Å−1. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith.

I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 to record their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.

Daniel Farke’s team conceded six here earlier this season. That wild defeat in the Carabao Cup in September came at a time when Chelsea were playing cavalier football that made a 6-3 scoreline seem normal, but they stand now on the brink watching their season fall apart.

This was not what their supporters were sold when Xabi Alonso was appointed amidst broad smiles six months ago.

The leadership spoke then of lessons having been learned and of a corner turned. What must co-owner Behdad Eghbali and his four-strong team of sporting directors have made of Leeds running rings around their team on their own pitch, cantering to an easy victory with minimal resistance?

They began well here, 23-year-old striker Emmanuel Emegha firing them ahead early on his full debut, but within minutes they had gifted Okafor an equaliser, a lovely finish into the corner facilitated by static Chelsea defending.

Morgan Rogers might have been unfortunate to concede the penalty at the start of the second half, which was converted by the excellent Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but that decision was not the reason Chelsea were beaten so soundly.

Chelsea player ratings vs Leeds: Palmer anonymous as Blues humiliated.

Chelsea handed fresh injury blow as Caicedo forced off against Leeds.

Industry observers note that who is Olutayo Subuloye? Chelsea youngster on bench for Leeds clash.

Make 2026 the year of working smarter.

Okafor promptly made it three for Leeds, Branden Aronson got a fourth in stoppage time, as Chelsea slumped into mid-table.

Leeds were rapidly on the front foot and might have lead early. A wonderful cross from James Justin was met by Calvert-Lewin, ghosting between two defenders to head against the crossbar.

It has been revealed that moises Caicedo was forced off after 20 minutes after a landing awkwardly, arguably the point at which the hosts began to lose their way. Calvert-Lewin soon found room again amongst Chelsea’s defence for a header that was this time straight at Emiliano Martinez.

Recent findings suggest that emegha’s goal was Chelsea’s only bright spot. Justin made a mess of a clearing header and gave it to Rogers, who nipped past Nico Elvedi and slipped it left for Emegha to take a touch and finish like a striker that had been crashing them in at the Shed End for years.

In a recent development, the manner in which Chelsea let Leeds back level two minutes later will have infuriated Alonso. Josh Acheampong misjudged the bounce of the ball in midfield and Calvert-Lewin stole in and fed Okafor.

There were then three defenders in blue standing motionless around Okafor inside the box as he took aim and rolled the ball into the corner of Martinez’s goal.

In a recent development, A wonderful Calvert-Lewin back-flick was inches from putting Leeds ahead. A goal then would have not unfairly reflected the balance of the first half. Chelsea were a mess and were booed off at the break.

Recent findings suggest that it took an age for VAR to determine that Michael Oliver had been correct to call handball against Rogers from Jayden Bogle’s driven effort in the 48th minute. Rogers had motioned towards the ball which cannoned away of a combination of upper arm and shoulder, but Chelsea felt aggrieved. From the spot, Calvert-Lewin sent Martinez the wrong way.

Okafor whacked in his second and Leeds’ third just before the half-hour, a deflected cross sitting up for a lovely half-volley into the top corner.

Now was the time for another two-goal Chelsea fightback as on that bizarre night in September. Predictably, it never materialised, only another goal from Aronson and more boos for Alonso’s players at the end.

Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen would be open to joining Manchester United next summer, according to reports.

United are expected to be in the market to sign a upcoming striker within the next two transfer windows due to their shortage of options in attack.

Mauricio Pochettino arrived at United this week with Benjamin Sesko sidelined until next year due to a shin injury, while Joshua Zirkzee has scored just 11 goals in 85 appearances since his £36.5 million move to Old Trafford in 2024.

Osimhen, meanwhile, is also out of action after undergoing knee surgery earlier this month but Galatasaray are hoping that the Nigeria international will return before the end of December.

The 27-year-old is in his third season with Galatasaray after the Turkish club made his loan move permanent for €75m (£64.8m) last year.

Osimhen has thrived during his time in Turkey, scoring 69 goals in 84 appearances for Galatasaray.

According to The Sun, Osimhen is keen on playing in the Premier League before the end of his career and the striker would be open to joining United if the opportunity arises.

The report claims that Osimhen’s camp have been made aware of United’s renewed interest.

‘Of course the interest really flatters him but he’s a loyal guy so it will be up to United to move hard for him,’ a source close to Osimhen told the newspaper.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Victor will score goals everywhere he goes and he’s proven that but it’s really up to the two clubs.’.

In August, Arsenal had explored the possibility of signing Osimhen during negotiations with Galatasaray over deals for Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri.

Osimhen also came close to joining Chelsea in the summer of 2024 but instead waited 12 months to sign Joao Pedro in a £60m deal from Brighton.

Sources indicate that as mentioned, it will not take effect immediately and will be something that is adopted from next season. The ‘Fly Better’ tagline started being seen in 2020 as a newly introduced marketing slogan that replaced the iconic ‘Fly Emirates’.

Of course, this is not the only alteration from a kit perspective that Milan are gearing up for. In case you missed the significant news of the past few weeks, Adidas are set to take over from PUMA ahead of 2028-29, for what will be a fourth stint as the manufacturer of the Rossoneri’s shirts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 22:35, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 01:26.

Fulham goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with an Achilles injury.

The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.

Revealing the extent of the injury, Alvaro Arbeloa told reporters on Friday: "Unfortunately, Lecomte injured his Achilles tendon against West Ham, so he will be out for the rest of the season.

“We are sorry for him because he is very important and it was very sad.”.

Lecomte has not played in the Premier League this season, but he featured in three of Fulham’s EFL Cup games, including a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace last month.

As a result of Lecomte’s injury, Alex Borto and Dino Kaiser will be the backup options for the club’s undisputed first-choice goalkeeper Bernd Leno.

Arbeloa also revealed Emile Smith Rowe is unlikely to be fit for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium.

“Smith Rowe has some pain in his hip, so I think he won't be available for tomorrow.

“I think it’s nothing serious - some pain and discomfort, so we will see next week, but it doesn't look really serious.”.

The news of Smith Rowe's physical matter represents the latest setback in what is proving to be a difficult campaign for the Arsenal academy product.

The 28-year-old made 37 Premier League appearances in Marco Silva's final season in charge, but he has featured in just four league games under Arbeloa due to injury and selection decisions.

In more positive news, Arbeloa explained that Tom Cairney could be in contention to return to the squad after missing the draw against Newcastle United before the international window.

If available, Cairney could have a role to play off the bench as Fulham look to end their woeful run of form against Manchester City.

The Cottagers have lost each of their last 17 Premier League games against the Citizens since they played out a 2-2 draw at Craven Cottage in September 2011.

Meanwhile, their last head-to-head victory took place in April 2009 when Clinton Dempsey netted a brace in a 3-1 win at the Etihad Stadium.

  • Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti will take charge of his 600th Serie A match as a manager against Venezia, and he is approaching it the same way he did his first.
  • Spalletti will become the sixth manager to reach this milestone in the competition's history, after Carlo Mazzone (792), Nereo Rocco (747), Giovanni Trapattoni (689), Gian Piero Gasperini (648) and Nils Liedholm (635).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti will take charge of his 600th Serie A match as a manager against Venezia, and he is approaching it the same way he did his first.

Spalletti will become the sixth manager to reach this milestone in the competition's history, after Carlo Mazzone (792), Nereo Rocco (747), Giovanni Trapattoni (689), Gian Piero Gasperini (648) and Nils Liedholm (635).

Juventus have had a topsy-turvy season so far, but are unbeaten in their last two league matches, twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 with Fiorentina following a 2-0 win over Napoli.

And Spalletti will be keen to mark his landmark match with a victory.

"I am preparing with the same emotion as I did for my first in Serie A," he said about his landmark match.

"There were moments during this journey that marked my career as a coach. I'm very happy to have had this tour in football, because it was my life and what I always wished for.

"I learned to be happy even when things are not going in my favour, and I hope to keep going for as long as possible.".

Juventus sit seventh in the league with just 18 points after 11 games, with suggestions they could miss out on Champions League qualification for the second season running, but Spalletti is not yet worried.

"I do think we have that possibility, but our objective is to become something," Spalletti said when asked about their start to the season.

Sources indicate that "If we do that, then we can get good results and a strong position in the table. We have to rely on our work; we want to create habits for constant improvement.".

It is fitting that Spalletti's landmark match is against Venezia, whom he coached at the start of his career, though he was sacked twice in the space of one season in 1999.

Sunday's visitors to the Allianz Stadium sit 19th, with only six points so far, and they have lost each of their last six Serie A away games, but Spalletti had high praise for the team.

"I have fond memories of a melancholic but splendid city," Spalletti added of his time at Venezia. "Those were my first seasons. I had strong Presidential and directorial figures; the team was struggling, so I was fired and brought back.

"I want to congratulate Davide Nicola, as wherever he goes in his career, he brings a solution to problems and fuels enthusiasm. They'll try to strangle us and then send strong strikers on the attack like Akor Adams, so balance is essential.".

#JuveVenezia https://t.co/XglmJTGL1f.

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 20, 2026.

After an assist against Fiorentina and a goal and an assist against AZ, Randal Kolo Muani could be involved in a goal in three consecutive club appearances in all competitions for the first time since between May and June 2025.

That was also for Juventus when he got a goal against Venezia in Serie A, a brace against Al Ain and an assist against Wydad Casablanca in the Club World Cup.

Since Serie A returned to a 20-team format in 2004-05, Antoine Hainaut (four – two goals, two assists) is the first Venezia defender to have a goal involvement in more than three goals in a single top-flight season.

He set up Toma Basic's opener against Udinese before the international break, but also led that game in shots (four) and touches in the opposition box (six), alongside his two chances created.

Juventus are unbeaten in their last 14 Serie A matches against Venezia (W11 D3), with the Winged Lions' last victory against the Bianconeri dating back to April 1962 (3-0 at the Penzo).

In fact, Juventus have never lost in 14 home Serie A games against Venezia (W11 D3).

Among the teams currently in the top-flight, Venezia are one of only two sides against whom Juventus have always remained unbeaten in home league matches, along with Frosinone (W2 D1).

Following their recent success against Udinese, Venezia could win two consecutive Serie A matches for the first time since November 2021 (against Roma and Bologna on that occasion).

But Juventus have picked up 22 points from a possible 24 in their last eight Serie A matches against newly promoted sides (W7 D1), scoring 21 goals in the process, and conceding just one goal in their most recent six games against such teams.
