Industry observers note that greetings, Tim here on blog duty today and I am going right back to Arseblog’s roots by writing from Barcelona. I am here of course because Arsenal Women earned a very creditable (and slightly unexpected given how this season has gone for them) draw against the current Champions League holders Barcelona.

Industry observers note that of course, Renee Slegers’ side did beat Barca the last time the teams met in the 2025 Final and that was only slightly less of an upset than this result. As expected, Arsenal rose their luck a little with Barca putting up 24 shots and 2.4XG. But Arsenal have put up similar numbers in games this season roughly 176 times and not won so I am happy to be on the receiving end of a little serendipity.

Frida Maanum gave Arsenal a first half lead before her compatriot Caroline Graham Hansen equalised in the second half. You can read Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference here and my take on the match here if you are so inclined. Up next is a six pointer for Champions League qualification at home to London City Lionesses on Sunday which Arsenal just have to win. Obviously we will have all the usual coverage of that game for you.

I also had the pleasure of meeting fellow Arseblog / Arsenal Vision colleague Phil Costa for lunch and in Barcelona, for a seafood and beer lover, a long lunch in balmy 20 degree conditions was very welcome indeed!

Elsewhere, there were plenty of Arsenal players in action for their countries. Martin Zubimendi played the full 90 minutes for Spain in their 2-0 away win at Czechia. Usually I would wince at a sentence that featured ‘Arsenal player x’ and ‘full 90 minutes’ but I think Zubimendi could use those minutes for physical reasons and for psychological reasons as he tries to plot his way back into a very crowded Arsenal midfield.

Mikel Merino came on for the final 24 minutes of that game and David Raya kept his gloves clean on the bench. Declan Rice played 77 minutes of England’s 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley in which Harry Kane scored his 417th goal for England, 461 of which have been penalties (citation needed). Eze was an unused sub and he’s another I wouldn’t have minded seeing get some minutes to build rhythm and confidence.

It has been revealed that riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 of Italy’s 3-1 win over France. Jurrien Timber and Kai Havertz could be in action tonight as Netherlands play Greece and Germany play away at Serbia. Fingers crossed for both. These are two players I would not mind seeing unused but I doubt that will be the case.

Meanwhile, the big news elsewhere was that Michael Carrick was finally officially sacked by Manchester United. He had still been taking training this week despite everyone knowing that he was for the chop. I hope he filled his coat pockets with as many of the milk and ketchup sachets as he could from the canteen.

Sources indicate that he was clearly out of his depth and had been stalking the United dugout looking like a haunted Noel Gallagher for what feels like months. Steve Holland has also left and Ben White’s recent recall to the England team resurfaced old wounds as he was asked about his reasons for making himself unavailable for a while for his country. White refuses to be drawn on it.

I am biased, of course, but I know who I think has emerged better from this sorry saga and his surname is a colour not a country. Having taken in Spurs and Chelsea already, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is about to go three for three on his tour of the Premier League’s most evil institutions. If hell really does exist, this man will regard an eternal stint of fire and brimstone as something of a vacation. Maybe working for the Jim Reaper at United is his penance for accepting work from Chelsea and Spurs.

For further reading, check out my weekly column in which I look at three ways in which Arsenal have evolved this season.

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

Sources indicate that the three substantial guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the substantial three were on the difference was obvious.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta remarked. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW.

It has been revealed that arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

In a recent development, as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Recent findings suggest that lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#83646. An Arseblog update

An Arseblog update

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1155 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026.
  • It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts.
  • “Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026. I’m in my hotel room in London, doing a few Arseblog bits on my laptop, and getting ready for the launch of the The 22 in the Big Red that night.

My phone rings. It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts. Typically I wouldn’t answer, but I think I know who it probably is. I’m right. It’s the Oncology department of the hospital I was admitted to a couple of weeks ago. They have news.

“We have the results of your biopsy.”.

“Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”.

“Great, we’ll see you then. Oh, and you should bring somebody with you. It’s a lot of information to take in.”.

Recent findings suggest that as of this moment, I’m still not 100% on all the details. I had another scan yesterday, and I have a procedure scheduled for Tuesday which will give us more information. However, they’ve already laid out a strategy for three months of chemo, which is kind of why I’m writing this.

My very, very strong instinct with any medical stuff is to keep it private. And I suppose if I was a guy who had a regular 9 to 5 and went to the office every day, I could do that. However, the privilege of my work is that it is very public facing. I do the stuff, you read the stuff and listen to the stuff, and you are part of my life in a very major way; in the same way – even if it it’s just for a few minutes each morning, or a couple of hours in your headphones – that I’m part of yours.

Industry observers note that which isn’t say I feel like I owe anyone an explanation, but this is my reality now, and for what’s likely to be an arduous road ahead for a while. Unfortunately, that makes it part of your reality too. I will say, I’m not going to document my ‘journey’. Fair play to anyone who does. Whatever you need to do to get through the challenges an illness presents, it’s just not really who I am. I don’t even do video on podcasts about football, so I’m not gonna start now for something like this!

But I do need the distraction of work, of Arsenal, of football and all its ludicrousness and drama, and this incredible community that has grown over the near 25 years of Arseblog’s existence. I’ve missed it this week, despite the fact it’s been such a difficult time in this household. We’ve gone through all the normal human reactions and emotions, and the whole thing was compounded by the fact I came back from London with the single worst stomach bug I’ve ever had in my life. To be honest, that felt a bit mean from the universe. Here, have a bit of this, and just to make you feel worse, you will require about twenty visits to the bathroom every day. It’s a bit like one of those days where every set of traffic lights you hit turns red as you approach, but the traffic lights also make your arse hurt. Fuck off!

It has been revealed that so, I’m going to be around, and I’m gonna do my best to do what I normally do. I need as much normal as I can get, because right now too much isn’t. But there will be days when I’m not, or I can’t be, and I’m happy to let the lads pick up the slack as much as possible. To preempt many messages and thoughts, I know what the priority is, and I’m not going to push myself at the expense of my health or getting better. I have a vested interest in, you know, making a full recovery. I’m not going to risk doing anything that might conflict with that.

But I also feel like the best way to navigate this is to not let it take over my life, or to define who I am. I’m still just an Irish bloke with a website about Arsenal first and foremost, and the last week or so has made me feel strangely protective of that. A dose of perspective is a really interesting thing, I know what the most key thing is right now, but that can only succeed if I remain myself. I hope that makes sense.

Recent findings suggest that some lads kicking a ball around a football pitch is, in the grand scheme of things, not that important. But hasn’t that always been the case? Football is so intrinsic to all of us, and we give so much of our time and energy to it, because we (well most of us) understand the absurdity of giving so much of ourselves to something that is completely out of our control. We can pretend otherwise, but that’s all part of the fun too. Lucky socks and lucky shirts and matchday routines. Our brain’s way of trying to make it feel like we have some influence, because we need that sliver of pretence, but in the end it’s about whether some millionaire at the back post can apply the finish.

I suppose at least this shit waited until there was an Interlull. Thanks for that.

Sources indicate that I’m lucky because I have an amazing wife and daughter, and family and friends, who will be with me every step of the way. Their support thus far has been incredible, and I know I can count on it 100%. I’m going to listen to the doctors and the medical team and do whatever it is they ask of me. They seem to know what they’re on about, which is reassuring. Almost like they’re experts or something. We should listen to them.

I know as well that wider support from the Arseblog community will be forthcoming, and I just wanted to say in advance that I appreciate it hugely. I suspect that replying to every message is going to be beyond me, and in normal circumstances that would bother me greatly. I always try to respond to every email I get, even if it takes me a while, but in this instance I hope you’ll understand if I don’t or can’t.

So that’s where we are. I still don’t know where we’ll end up or how we’ll get there, but despite the fact I’m scared and worried, I’m also positive and determined. I could really do without this, to be quite honest, but it is what it is, and the only way through is forward. I’ll keep you in the loop as much as I feel I can, and in the meantime if Arsenal could make my day to day life as stress free as possible, I’d really appreciate that.

Someone have a word with Mikel and the lads.

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 12:28.

Ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash between Newcastle United and Arsenal, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton warns Mikel Arteta to expect a "horrible" evening at St James' Park.

According to recent reports, newcastle vs. Arsenal is just always one of those really awkward fixtures. The only two modern wins I can remember in the current decade were towards the end of the 2022-23 season and of course last season, that magnificent Merino and Gabriel comeback.

Industry observers note that apart from that, St. James' Park has been a pretty hellish ground for Arsenal. But the stats do not lie this season.

Five points clear at the top, nine wins from 10. Only four teams have had a better start than Arsenal's 27 points from 30: Chelsea in 2005-06, City in 2011-12, City in 2017-18, and Liverpool in 2019-20.

All four of those teams went on to win the title.

By that logic, I think this is Arsenal's title to lose, though perhaps too early to say that definitively.

Arsenal fans should be overwhelmingly happy, but there is always that sense we want more. So many of the wins have been narrow, one-nil victories. The Nottingham Forest win needed a deflected goal. The Hull win needed a rebound.

Hull set up in that 5-4-1 deep block, and Arsenal got a little fortuitous, but they also did not get a penalty that the key match incidents panel later said we should have had.

I was also frustrated at Noni Madueke for spurning that late one-on-one chance. He got caught in two minds going around the goalkeeper, when he should have tried to curl it into the bottom corner.

He was clearly upset with himself afterwards. That said, I do not want to be too critical of Madueke right now, because with Dowman still out suspended, Saka still out injured, Madueke has come to the fore in recent weeks.

He has not hit those same numbers that Saka was putting up a couple of years ago at his peak, but many aspects of his game have come on significantly.

He will start on the right-hand side here, and the Madueke versus Lewis Hall battle will be a fascinating one to watch.

According to recent reports, but above all else, Arsenal just need to start blowing teams away. Arteta remarked as much after the Hull City win. He now has 34 1-0 wins in the Premier League since taking charge, the most of any manager in that period.

Industry observers note that arsenal have only scored five goals in their five away games, so I would not be surprised to see another 1-0 here. I am confident for an Arsenal win, but at St. James' Park there is always that hint of fear.

Under the lights, if the team and the fans get going, it can be a horrible place to visit as an Arsenal fan.

Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January plans

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (489 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Juvefc

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it.
  • Recent findings suggest that juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in newly introduced capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November.
  • In a recent development, part of the money is already committed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Recent findings suggest that juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in newly introduced capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

In a recent development, part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its newly introduced authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

Recent findings suggest that the squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

According to recent reports, the accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

Recent findings suggest that the assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious firm, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

In a recent development, shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

According to recent reports, the terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

Opinion: Liverpool ready to sign their next Jeremy Jacquet, he's perfect

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The young Frenchman was brought in for around £55 million with plenty of fans, pundits and journalists all saying that Liverpool had spent too much on a player who'd never played outside of France.
  • The fact that he was only 20 years old didn't help matters much either.
  • However, to the surprise of many, he took becoming a Liverpool player in his stride and has arguably been one of their best performers this term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jeremy Jacquet has been a revelation at Liverpool.

The young Frenchman was brought in for around £55 million with plenty of fans, pundits and journalists all saying that Liverpool had spent too much on a player who'd never played outside of France.

The fact that he was only 20 years old didn't help matters much either.

However, to the surprise of many, he took becoming a Liverpool player in his stride and has arguably been one of their best performers this term.

He's far better than Ibrahima Konate ever was and, he's still got another decade left as a top-level player.

So, the fact that Liverpool are ready to sign their next version of him is rather exciting.

Liverpool have entered the transfer race for Giorgio Scalvini.

Liverpool's defence may have had a decent chunk of change spent on it over the last couple of years but, there are still a couple of problem areas that they need to fix.

For example, both Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez have massively underperformed this season.

Every time one of them is played, fans want the other to come back in and take their place.

Obviously, this isn't ideal considering Kerkez was expected to be the Reds' next Andy Robertson.

However, the centre of their defence also has a couple of question marks hanging over it thanks to the undecided futures of Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez.

So, Liverpool being linked with Giorgio Scalvini is hardly a surprised, especially with how much potential he has to fulfil.

"Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea are positioning themselves to make a possible move for Atalanta defensive star Giorgio Scalvini, with the highly-rated Italian emerging as a major potential transfer target for 2027, TEAMtalk can exclusively reveal," TEAMtalk wrote.

"TEAMtalk understands that a number of English sides are now carrying out detailed work on Scalvini as the possibility of him finally leaving Atalanta gathers momentum.

"Newcastle United are long-term admirers of the Italy international, but the latest interest is coming from Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea, who have all been monitoring his development.

"United and Liverpool are both assessing their central defensive options as they consider potential reinforcements, with Scalvini increasingly emerging as a player of interest to their recruitment departments.".

Giorgio Scalvini could become Liverpool's next Jeremy Jacquet.

Scalvini has been linked with an exit from Atalanta for a fair few years now.

Ever since he broke into their first team back in the 2021/22 season, the Italian has been of interest to many different clubs around the globe.

However, now that Liverpool have proven that they're giving youngsters a go in their starting XI with their use of Jacquet and others such as Trey Nyoni, they have more ground to stand on than other clubs.

Of course, Scalvini is a tad older than Jacquet at 22 years old but, since they're both young and have a lot of their careers left to go, it's clear to see why the Italian could become Liverpool's next Jacquet.

He also plays as the right-sided centre-back in a back four so, he'd fit straight into Andoni Iraola's plans if they chose to bring him in.

It’ll be Ben White on the night

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid.
  • Obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England.
  • Holland was the one who sparked the issue originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid. Ezri Konsa made it 2-0 with a close range header, Spain might wonder who was marking him (I think it was supposed to be Marc Cucurella) but the movement was really sharp. Then a couple of minute later, Ben White fired England into a 3-0 lead, with Cucurella also in close attendance.

Obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England. The worst sections of the media have fanned the flames against him, and it doesn’t take much to rile up those who are already of a jingoistic persuasion. As we’ve seen since seen with stories about Steve Holland being hugely unpopular at Man Utd, there’s a common denominator, and it’s not Ben White.

Holland was the one who sparked the issue originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick. I also feel quite confident that even if there is a cohort who won’t forgive Ben White for the crime of Steve Holland being a dickhead, he probably won’t care too much. Look at the reactions of his teammates and manager to the goal, and that’s tells you plenty.

He was also involved in a minor scuffle going off at half-time, which also seemed to involved Konsa and Martin Zubimendi, but I’m sure it was just heat of the moment stuff. Although Spain got two back after England went down to 10 men, they made the fatal mistake of starting Mikel Merino. How was he supposed to come off the bench and get a vital goal then? Silly Luis de la Fuenta, bloke’s a fraud.

Industry observers note that elsewhere over the weekend, Viktor Gyokeres scored twice for Sweden, both from the penalty spot. We just need more penalties. This is the key to unlocking him. Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 as Italy went down 4-1 to Belgium (ouch), Martin Odegaard played 90 as Norway beat Wales, and there are some more games to come this week with Germany facing Netherlands tonight (Kai v Timber), the Brazilians are in action in Singapore, and apparently Christos Tzolis is fit to play for Greece after having an MRI.

Recent findings suggest that maybe it’s my own recent experiences, but I don’t care for the idea he needs an MRI. I get it, it’s probably for his knee or hamstring or something, but it feels like if you need one of those to know if you’re fit, you’re probably not feeling 100% anyway. I guess this will be one Mikel Arteta will keep a close eye on tonight when Greece host Serbia and Tzolis inevitably starts. Ideally, these will be useful minutes for him, and help him deliver for us but you can’t help but worry considering he picked up an injury in the last Interlull.

Sources indicate that finally for today, it looks as if a Declan Rice contract extension is close. Speaking while on England duty, he stated:.

In a recent development, “A upcoming contract is hopefully on the horizon soon. I’m extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager demonstrates me so much trust and teammates who put so much energy and effort into to me.

“I’m extremely lucky not to have to worry about that stuff, and it makes playing football far more easier.”.

This is, by any measure, a no-brainer. I don’t think there’s a club in the world that would turn him down if he were available, and his importance to Arsenal is just obvious. In a world when £100m+ transfers often struggle to provide value, this is one of the exceptions. If you went back to 2023 and had to do it all again, even if you added another £20m or £30m to the fee we paid West Ham, it would be worth it. It’s likely to be the kind of deal that sees him play out the rest of his prime years in red and white, and let’s hope there are more trophies along the way to accompany that.

Industry observers note that right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

It has been revealed that the pod should be out around around midday. Until then, have a good one – after which I’m gonna be off for a couple of days but the lads will keep things ticking here until I get back.

Published: 11:37 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 20 November 2026.

Sources indicate that derek McInnes can be understood in wanting a quiet January window. He’s still bonding a squad of players together. Drama and diversions are the last thing he needs when there looks to be an opportunity to win a title on the horizon.

In the case of Olwethu Makhanya, for example, this is definitely not the time to sell.

The 22-year-old South African has been impressive at centre-back, but it will take a campaign catching the attention in high-level European football for him to raise his value to Calvin Bassey levels and beyond.

In a recent development, same goes for the likes of Ryan Naderi. Getting into the Czechia squad and increasing his range of experience makes him a more interesting prospect, but UEFA competition is a platform that ought to increase his premium.

According to recent reports, mcInnes, as he did this week, has to say he wants to keep his more prominent talents anyway. It would be strange to appear accepting of the board cashing in on bigger players.

It has been revealed that when it comes to Nico Raskin, however, things are different. A buyer for him should have been found in the summer after his World Cup involvement with Belgium.

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin is an asset who could be sold in the January transfer window.

From the chit-chat around the game, it does not seem unreasonable to think Rangers maybe overvalued him in the initial part of that window and missed the boat in terms of securing a sale.

If he stays for the rest of this season and enters the final year of his contract, though, the money you can ask for naturally reduces. The club might seek to tie him up on a fresh deal, of course, but his remarks about being ‘mentally ready to leave’ at the start of the season point to the most likely direction of travel.

Is he irreplaceable? Not at all. And this is where forward planning should come into the mix.

If there’s someone out there willing to edge anywhere close to the £15m mark for the 25-year-old, they should be getting sounded out now – with a contingency plan being discussed and worked on in tandem.

Yes, Rangers need to get back to winning silverware, but the need to start raising funds through selling players – and replacing them - at appropriate times is pressing too.

As often mentioned here, they can’t keep spending money the way they have been without considerably more coming back in return.

Recent findings suggest that raskin’s a good player, but his three-and-a-half years at Ibrox have hardly been shaped by his propensity for winning medals, have they? If a realistic fee is there in January, there’s a case to make for it being taken.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that juventus won 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar on a night when Teun Koopmeiners faced his old club, even though the hosts dominated the expected-goals count. The result strengthens their league-phase position ahead of Sunday's Serie A trip to Fiorentina.

Industry observers note that the trip to Alkmaar returned Teun Koopmeiners to his former club. His brother Peer was in the AZ side that Juventus then held off. UEFA picked out the family meeting in its matchday 4 round-up.

Koopmeiners opened the scoring in the 19th minute from a Kolo Muani pass. Kolo Muani doubled the lead in the 37th minute, with Nick Woltemade credited with the assist, and Juventus led 2-0 at half-time. Kolo Muani earned a rating of 8.61 from the data provider, with Koopmeiners on 8.2.

Recent findings suggest that AZ pulled one back in the 88th minute. Mexx Meerdink scored from an Elijah Dijkstra assist. The hosts could not find an equaliser in the remaining minutes.

Industry observers note that the home side had 56% of possession. They completed 523 passes to Juventus’s 378. Eleven of AZ’s attempts were blocked, against three of Juventus’s.

Both teams put three shots on target. Vicario made two saves for Juventus. AZ’s expected goals total points to the chances the hosts created without converting them.

In a recent development, the figures are consistent with a Juventus side defending a first-half lead. Spalletti’s team committed 20 fouls to AZ’s 13. Andrea Cambiaso, Jeff Ekhator and Juan Cabal were booked for Juventus. Wesley Hoedt was the only AZ player shown a yellow card. Damian Sylwestrzak refereed the match.

According to recent reports, the victory was Spalletti’s second in a row in all competitions, following the league win over Napoli. It came after a run that included a 0-2 defeat to Genoa and a 0-3 loss to Lazio. This season’s league phase has 36 clubs, and each plays eight different opponents. It ends on Thursday 28 January 2027. Paris FC vs Angers - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Nsidibe Akpan | 21 Nov 2026 12:38.
  • Third-placed Paris FC welcome Angers SCO to the Stade Jean Bouin in Ligue 1 on Sunday, with kick-off at 3pm local time.
  • The hosts have won four and drawn one of their five home league games, while the visitors are winless in five and sit 17th after Troyes beat Le Havre 3-1 on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 21 Nov 2026 12:38.

Third-placed Paris FC welcome Angers SCO to the Stade Jean Bouin in Ligue 1 on Sunday, with kick-off at 3pm local time.

The hosts have won four and drawn one of their five home league games, while the visitors are winless in five and sit 17th after Troyes beat Le Havre 3-1 on Friday.

Paris FC have taken 20 points from 10 league games, with six wins, two draws and two defeats, leaving them behind only Paris Saint-Germain on 23 points and Lille on 21 on the Ligue 1 table before the leaders play on Saturday.

Liam Rosenior was appointed on July 7 on a contract running to June 2028, after a 107-day spell at Chelsea that ended with his sacking in April, and his side have scored 17 goals and conceded 10.

The standout figure is Lassine Sinayoko, who joined from Auxerre in the summer and leads the division with nine goals in 10 league games, three of them penalties, to go with five assists.

Sinayoko scored a hat-trick in the 3-2 win at Marseille on matchday three, added two goals and an assist in the 3-1 victory over Monaco on November 1, and then scored the only goal at his former club Auxerre on November 7, with Pablo Pagis providing the pass.

Jean Bouin has been the foundation of the season, as Paris FC are unbeaten at home in the league with four wins and a goalless draw against Lyon, scoring 12 goals and conceding five, and they have now gone seven consecutive matches there without defeat.

Their two league defeats came at Lorient (1-0 on October 10) and Lens (2-1 on October 24), and Rosenior said after the Lorient game that his players had never faced such a low block, which is the one test Angers could realistically set.

Angers have eight points from 10 games after two wins, two draws and six defeats, which leaves them six points clear of bottom side Le Havre, who have lost seven in a row.

Their wins came in a 3-1 victory at Auxerre on August 29 and a 2-0 home win over Troyes on September 19, and since the Troyes game they have drawn 0-0 with Lorient and lost four of five, scoring three goals and conceding 14.

The damage was done by two heavy defeats in a short space of time, a 5-1 loss at Brest on October 10, when Brest posted an expected-goals figure of 3.71 against Angers’ 1.39 and Jordan Lefort was sent off, and a 5-2 home defeat against Marseille on October 18.

The 2-0 loss at home to Nice on November 8 was a different problem, as Sofiane Diop scored in the second minute and Angers created so little that goalkeeper Anthony Lopes, a 35-year-old who joined after Nantes were relegated, needed six saves to prevent a heavier scoreline.

Stephane Gilli returns to the club he coached from July 2023 until his dismissal on February 22, when Paris FC were 15th, and he was appointed by Angers on June 9 on a deal to 2028 after Alexandre Dujeux left for Lorient.

Gilli has said Angers will adjust defensively without changing everything and that emotion will play no part on Sunday, but his attack has failed to score in five of 10 league matches, with Prosper Peter scoring against Troyes and Brest and Amine El Ouazzani against Troyes.

Paris FC will be without Jonathan Ikone, who has a dead leg, and Nhoa Sangui, who has a muscle injury, and neither is expected back until late November, while Adama Camara (hamstring) and Samir Chergui (knock) are doubts.

Rosenior otherwise has a near-complete squad, and at Auxerre he used a back three of Hamari Traore, Otavio and Diego Coppola, with Coppola rated the man of the match by Maxifoot.

Moses Simon and Rudy Matondo provided the width at Auxerre, with Ilan Kebbal and Pagis supporting Sinayoko, who is expected to lead the line again.

Angers will be without Lefort, who is suspended, and Bane Diatta, who is injured, while Oumar Pona was ruled out after falling ill on his return from Mali Under-23 duty.

El Ouazzani is available after returning from injury, and Ousmane Camara and Amine Sbai both took part in training on Friday after being rested on Thursday.

With Lefort suspended, Emmanuel Biumla is expected to partner Camara in central defence, with Carlens Arcus and Kalulu at full-back in front of Lopes.

Paris FC possible starting lineup:.

Trapp; Traore, Otavio, Coppola; Simon, Lopez, Lees-Melou, Matondo; Kebbal, Pagis; Sinayoko.

Angers possible starting lineup:.

Lopes; Arcus, Camara, Biumla, Kalulu; Belkhdim, Belkebla; Allevinah, van den Boomen, Sbai; Peter.

Paris FC have scored 12 goals in five home league matches while Angers have conceded 14 in their last five, and that gap in output makes a home win the logical outcome.

Sinayoko decided the last two league wins, with two goals against Monaco and the winner at Auxerre, and an Angers back line without Lefort will have to deal with him for 90 minutes.

The counter-argument is that Angers beat Paris FC 1-0 in August 2025 and held them 0-0 at Jean Bouin in January, and that Rosenior’s side needed until the 63rd minute to break down a 5-4-1 Auxerre.

Those meetings, however, came when Gilli was still in the Paris FC dugout, and this Angers side has been opened up repeatedly at Brest and Marseille and has scored only three goals in five games.

Lopes should keep the margin respectable, but a side that has failed to score in five of 10 league games is more likely to be shut out than to find a way past Kevin Trapp.

Divine Dowman does it again

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again.
  • Sources indicate that I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week.
  • It’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again. I suppose after 24 years of writing this blog, a few bad habits are bound to creep in….

Sources indicate that I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week. Fortunately, a lifetime of watching Arsenal has given me plenty of practice at making bad jokes when I don’t know what else to say.

It’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend. Bluesky, Reddit, X, Discord, Facebook, Patreon. Wherever I looked, there you were, sending love to Blogs. It was beautiful to see.

And to the handful of you who got in touch with me or people I know because you thought Friday’s enhancement was about my health, please hold that thought. I’m fine. Touch wood. There are, in fact, two Andrews at Arseblog, and I’m the other one.

Having been crowned the “World’s Youngest Boy” by James on yesterday’s Arsecast Extra, Max Dowman set yet another record last night, becoming England under-21s’ youngest scorer with the winner in a 3-2 victory over France in filthy conditions in Bristol.

It has been revealed that I’d planned to watch from kick-off, but gave up when I realised the game wasn’t on any of the 5,000 channels I pay £150 a month for. Then I saw on social media that Ethan Nwaneri, playing as a number 10, had laid on a couple of goals. So I did the clever thing and googled it. Turns out I needed the official England app and an account. Eyes still rolling, I tried to set up a login, only to find out I already had one. Cue the password reset process, verification codes and me losing the will to live. Just let me watch some fucking children play football in the rain!

It has been revealed that by the time I got the stream, it was nearly half-time. At least that gave me a chance to catch up on Nwaneri’s two assists, both of which were Ozil-esque. First he drove down the left and slipped a neat ball inside for Mikey Moore, right now on loan at Cologne, to finish. Then came a teasing dink to the back post that Southampton’s Divin Mubama met first time. Given how little Nwaneri has played for Dortmund lately, it was a welcome reminder of what he can do.

It feels a bit silly to say Max, who was named player of the match, looked comfortable at this level when he’s already got a Premier League winners’ medal next to his GCSE textbooks, but he really did.

Recent findings suggest that watching him is like reading someone’s really nice handwriting. Even the everyday stuff looks lovely. A touch to bring the ball under control, a little turn, and suddenly the defender who was right up his arse is looking at the back of his shirt. I’ll never get tired of watching him do that.

Industry observers note that as both sides made changes, I expected Lee Carsley to take him off. Instead, he played the full 90 and dug Arsenal teammate Tommy Setford out of a hole. The goalkeeper was at fault for the only goal in Friday’s defeat to Portugal and had another difficult night, spilling a cross into his own net. The rain hardly helped, and the 20-year-old has been doing well on loan at Stevenage, but it was a horrible one to concede.

When Brest’s Giovani Versini whipped in an equaliser with five minutes left, it looked like England would have to settle for a draw, but Dowman’s tap-in settled it with a minute to spare. Who knows, Dowman and Nwaneri could be on the same pitch again next week when Dortmund visit the Emirates.

Elsewhere, Group 2 of League A of the UEFA Nations League (catchy naming scheme, lads) served up another bonkers evening. Jurrien Timber scored twice in the Netherlands’ 7-0 win over Christos Tzolis’ Greece on Friday, only for the Dutch to lose 5-0 to Kai Havertz’s Germany in Berlin. There were some lovely goals from the Germans – including two from Florian Wirtz – who are finding their feet under Jurgen Klopp. Timber and Havertz both came off midway through the second half, seemingly unscathed. Timber’s pride aside, anyway.

Industry observers note that tzolis, meanwhile, was cleared to play after an MRI scan and got through 88 minutes of Greece’s 1-0 win over Serbia. All three sides finished on 11 points, with Germany and the Netherlands going through on goal difference at Greece’s expense.

Tonight, Martin Odegaard’s Norway face Denmark, while Viktor Gyokeres will look to extend his record-breaking scoring run for Sweden away at Poland. Piero Hincapie’s Ecuador take on Bolivia, Big Gabi and Bruno are in Singapore with Brazil, and Cristhian Mosquera and Marli Salmon are in action for Spain under-21s and England under-19s, respectively.

Sources indicate that closer to home, The Athletic ran two Arsenal contract stories in quick succession. James reports that Timber has agreed a fresh long-term deal, while David Ornstein indicates Declan Rice’s extension will take him through to 2031. Arsenal already had the option to keep Rice until 2029, so the new deal effectively buys them two more years and gives him a sizeable pay rise for the next four and a half. If he keeps playing as he has been, I can’t imagine many Arsenal fans quibbling with that.

For what it’s worth, we’ve heard on the grapevine that David Raya’s upcoming contract is all but done, too, which means the club are making good progress with the lads whose deals expire in 2028, a list that also includes Odegaard, Havertz, Mikel Merino and our two backup keepers.

There was an interesting discussion on Arsenal Vision’s ‘Friday Night Clive’ podcast about Arsenal elongating their “winning window” while having one eye on the next iteration of the team. If you hand expensive new contracts to players hurtling towards their thirties, you leave yourself financially exposed and potentially blocking pathways for up-and-coming talent. No doubt the club and manager are keenly aware of that. I just wonder how much you can expect the latter to focus on the faraway future when the dynasty he craves has to start in the here and now.

If this week has taught me anything, it’s that there’s something to be said for seizing the day. Admittedly, that’s easier when it’s Arsenal’s money I’m volunteering to spend.

If you’re about to part with some of your own (smooth segue, Allen) this year’s Arseblog Christmas Gift Guide is up.

Sources indicate that I spent some of last week rounding up Arsenal bits and pieces I’d be happy to find under the tree. Mostly, I wanted to point you towards the independent makers, artists and writers producing stuff I like. In many cases, what I’ve picked is just a small sample of what they do, so have a nose around.

If you’ve got a recommendation of your own, pop the link in the form at the bottom and I’ll take a look.

Right, I’d better crack on with the day job. Lewis is on duty tomorrow and, all being well, Andrew M should be back here before the week is out.

Good morning! I’ve got to say, if I worked at Arsenal and I wasn’t getting a new contract this international break, I think I’d be taking it pretty personally.

After Monday’s news that both Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice have agreed new deals with the club, Tuesday brought the news that fellow 2023 signing David Raya was next in line, swiftly followed by reports that Riccardo Calafiori will also be handed a new deal, and Piero Hincapie will be getting improved terms, too.

According to recent reports, since the end of the 2024-25 season, there have already been new deals for Gabriel, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri, William Saliba, Bukayo Saka, and, of course, Mikel Arteta. With the latest raft of agreements on top of those, that’s a lot of important people tied down for the next few years.

These deals will mean everyone other than Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Ben White, Mikel Merino, and Kepa is contracted to the club until at least 2029. That’s a nice feeling, isn’t it? There will be some decisions to be made over a couple of those players and whether it’s time to refresh, you’d imagine, but the bulk of the squad should be staying put and continuing to compete together – with a couple of additions supplementing them, of course – for the next couple of years at least.

Of those four (plus Kepa) mentioned above, you’d have to think Odegaard is the next priority when it comes to renewals, given his importance on and off the pitch and his current form.

I was in a bar here in Berlin catching up with a fellow Arsenal fan yesterday evening (hello, if you’re reading!) and they had Norway’s game in Denmark on. It’s fair to say the skipper continued his fine start to the season.

After Norway went two down against the run of play, Odegaard sprung into action. No player had as many touches on the night, and he was involved in all three Norway goals.

It has been revealed that he stole the ball for the goal that made it 2-1, which, by the way, we should have a word for. We have the word equaliser for when it goes to 2-2, but we don’t have a word for the goal that shortens the lead. The Germans call it an Anschlusstor – literally a ‘connecting goal’, the goal that means the scores are now just one apart.

Industry observers note that anyway, Odegaard, pressing as he always does, stole the ball from goalkeeper Mads Hermansen, then selflessly left the tap-in for Erling Haaland. He then scored the equaliser, a goal reminiscent of his opening day strike against Coventry if we’re honest: he didn’t hit it well, he got a bit lucky. But: right place, right time and all that.

And, finally, it was Odegaard’s ferociously whipped in free-kick that struck the hand of Joachim Andersen and allowed Haaland to convert from the penalty spot late into added time. If you’ve got a few minutes, you can see the highlights of his performance here – some of the touches are more than worth your time.

A good night’s work, especially after he was suffering with a stomach bug last week.

It wasn’t just the captain in action yesterday, either. Piero Hincapie played just over an hour for Ecuador overnight, there were assists for Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes as Brazil beat Singapore 7-0 earlier on in the day, and then an assist for Viktor Gyokeres too as Sweden drew with Poland.

Sources indicate that that looks like something he’s clearly worked on – getting his body in the way of the defender and, rather than holding the ball up, looking to direct it towards an oncoming runner. His assist for Declan Rice in Munich obviously looked pretty similar, and it’s not something we saw too much of last season.

Industry observers note that in fact, I thought I’d have a quick look, and Gyokeres has 13 key passes (a pass that leads a shot from a team-mate) in the Premier League and Champions League this season. He’s delivering a key pass every 28.4 minutes. Last season he had a key pass every 104 minutes across those two competitions. It’s hard not to conclude that he’s been working on that side of his game, and these Giroud-esque back-to-goal touches for team-mates are more than welcome.

It has been revealed that so, plenty of assists this break. Now we just need to harness that at Newcastle on Saturday and actually have someone to stick the ball in the back of the net at the end of those moves. Thankfully – knock on wood – it seems the players have made it through the break unscathed (there was also another behind-closed-doors appearance for William Saliba – a nod to Tom Canton for that story) and should be raring to go.

Industry observers note that lastly, I want to point you towards Arseblog News, where Andrew A wrote something last night on the death of double-winner Peter Storey, one of just eight players to make over 500 appearances for the club. That first double is such an enormous part of our history wouldn’t have happened without Storey’s nerves of steel in the FA Cup semi-final.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the Interlull is over and that’s it now until March.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, andrew M here after a couple of days ‘off’, but not the kind where you sit in a hammock and have delicious things brought to you. More the kind where you have three stab wounds in your abdomen and a chunk of your insides taken out. If at all possible, I seriously recommend the former to the latter. Anyway, I’m here right now with coffee and painkillers, which I guess is something akin to Arseblog heritage.

According to recent reports, the Interlull is over and that’s it now until March. It’s non-stop Arsenal all the way, and all the focus will be on us and what we can produce on the pitch. For those interested in what our players got up to during this break, and what they delivered for their respective nations, Andrew A has a handy round-up over on Arseblog News. Now it’s about keeping everyone as fit as possible, the manager using the squad in the smartest and most effective way he can, and for some of the players who are capable of producing more doing exactly that.

I was quite interested in Lewis’ quick look at Viktor Gyokeres and his key pass metrics from yesterday’s blog: He’s delivering a key pass every 28.4 minutes. Last season he had a key pass every 104 minutes across those two competitions [PL & CL].

I think sample size might be a factor here, because when you look at his xG per 90, it’s 0.05 per 90 in both Premier League and Champions League this season, versus .99 and .76 per 90 last season, but obviously he played more minutes last time out. After 14 appearances this season, he’s rustled up a total of 614 minutes; this time last season his first 14 appearances brought him a cumulative 1200+ minutes. The absence of Kai Havertz was a factor, obviously, but it was probably that early season load that contributed to the injury he picked up against Burnley after a solid first half performance.

The job for Mikel Arteta is to find a way to share those minutes effectively, to have both his strikers scoring and assisting, and to harness some of what Gyokeres has been able to produce for Sweden. It’s often mooted that as a team we need to play to his strengths more, but perhaps these key pass metrics show that the design is more about eliminating some of the weaknesses in his game to make him more effective in the final third for us. Let’s see how it goes.

Meanwhile, the KMI (Key Match Incident) panel have ruled on the Kai Havertz penalty incident against Hull. They ruled 5-0 that the on-field decision was wrong and that VAR, manned that day by Michael Oliver, should have intervened:.

Although Havertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence by Havertz. Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded. The panel considered the VAR intervention was correct; however, the outcome after the on-field review was considered to be incorrect as a penalty should have been awarded.

According to recent reports, I get every day is a learning day for ‘ProRef’, the people whose job it is to know the rules of football but week after week seem to demonstrate in new and inventive ways that they don’t. The question for us as fans is, what are we supposed to do with this? Are we supposed to feel better knowing that they’re owning up to mistakes? It feels a bit like getting run over when you have the green light at a pedestrian crossing, a nearby cop just lets the bloke go, but then later a judge claims he should have been stopped and arrested.

Sources indicate that which is all well and good when you’re in a hospital bed in traction with a couple of broken legs and smashed pelvis (I say this only because I remember being in hospital with a bloke who fell under a bus and that’s what happened to him. He was fine though, his mates brought him in loads of joints which he used to share in the smoking room – this was 90s hospital). Which is to say, the damage has been done, the admission the bloke got it wrong in the first place doesn’t really make you feel any better.

In a recent development, from our perspective at least, Martin Odegaard’s winner ensured that decision didn’t turn out to be one which went on to live in infamy – like not drawing the lines for that Brentford goal that time, but it’s still essentially useless. Not least because you just know this weekend or next weekend some other mad thing will happen and they’ll say ‘Oooops! Sorry about that LOL here’s Michael Owen and Howard Webb!’, and some team will lose points because they can’t properly apply the rules of the game to things that happen on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that finally for today, we’re being linked with a January move for Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott. He’s certainly a fine player, but it doesn’t make a lot of sense to me given we already have the best midfield depth in the Premier League, and beyond. Where does he fit with Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard? Perhaps if, for example, Zubi went there’s a case to be made for a replacement, but as it is he’s struggling for minutes anyway, and you don’t pay that kind of money for someone to come in and be peripheral.

Like most of you, if there’s money to be spent in January, I’d much rather see it go on the forward line where I feel like there’s obvious room for improvement and to increase our depth. The left hand side is the obvious place, it’s hard not to worry about the right a little bit with Bukayo Saka’s injury, and the striker conversation is one which is never quite going to go away. So, on that basis, links to Scott don’t really add up for me. Unless Arteta fancies converting him to another left-back. Then it all clicks, but I think there’s one Bournemouth player we’d all rather see arrive.

Industry observers note that right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. In terms of a podcast, I’m not quite feeling up to it today, but what we’ll do is make our Patreon preview podcast free and available to everyone tomorrow afternoon. I should be less sore then, and I continue to be blown away by your many emails and messages. Thank you so much, they mean the world.

Process of Elimination

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the course of the November international break, news of contract extensions for some of Arsenal’s ‘pillar’ players has begun to filter through.
  • Arsenal have assembled an elite core and it didn’t happen overnight.
  • Sources indicate that in hindsight, it’s interesting that only Ben White and Martin Odegaard have ‘survived’ since then, with Ramsdale, Tomiyasu, Lokonga and Tavares all having drifted away ever since.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the course of the November international break, news of contract extensions for some of Arsenal’s ‘pillar’ players has begun to filter through. David Raya, Jurrien Timber, Declan Rice and Piero Hincapie are all reportedly on the verge of new deals, with Riccardo Calafiori’s deal also in the in-tray for Andrea Berta too.

Arsenal have assembled an elite core and it didn’t happen overnight. Back in the summer of 2021, the club enacted a policy of buying players under 24 years old. I always felt like this was the true year zero of the Arteta project. That always felt like the window that built the foundations.

Sources indicate that in hindsight, it’s interesting that only Ben White and Martin Odegaard have ‘survived’ since then, with Ramsdale, Tomiyasu, Lokonga and Tavares all having drifted away ever since. Emile Smith Rowe also signed a latest contract and took the number 10 shirt that summer and now he is scratching around for minutes at Fulham.

The summer of 2022 saw the arrivals of Gabriel Jesus and Alex Zinchenko, as well as Fabio Vieira. The former pair briefly elevated Arsenal to a fresh level before becoming promptly obsolete. Vieira was a fairly pricey gamble that didn’t pay off. It was the summer of 2023 that truly established Arsenal among England’s elite. David Raya, Jurrien Timber, Declan Rice and Kai Havertz’s arrivals turned Arsenal from caterpillars to butterflies.

According to recent reports, three of those players are about to sign latest contracts. Curiously, we have little to no reporting on whether Kai Havertz is lined up for a new deal as yet. Arsenal are banking on their well assembled core to deliver more silverware as they enter their peak years (Raya is 31 which feels close to peak age for a goalkeeper).

It has been revealed that undoubtedly, there are some players who will drift away in the coming years. Mikel Merino, Martin Zubimendi and Ben White feel unlikely to get new Arsenal contracts at this particular moment in time. (Though these things can and do change). Like Havertz, Odegaard’s deal runs until the summer of 2028 and we have yet to hear rumblings of a new deal.

In a recent development, odegaard and Havertz have negotiated significant fitness challenges over the last two seasons, which probably explains why they have found themselves lower down Berta’s to do list. Timber has had his own physical challenges too, but he is 25. Havertz and Odegaard are 27. Their next contracts will be their last ‘significant’ contracts in terms of wages and their resale value will drop to close to zero if Arsenal tie them down. It makes sense for the club to take its time a little more with both players.

In a recent development, both are also defining attacking and / or creative players in the Arsenal team. At some point, Arteta is going to have to plot an evolution within this core and it feels like that is more likely to happen in the final third of the pitch than within the core of players who operate behind the ball. Behind the ball, Arsenal are absolutely tip top and have some of the most elite players in the world in their positions.

According to recent reports, that is not as true ahead of the ball. Odegaard and Havertz remain, for my money, elite, defining players for Arsenal. For the purposes of this piece; I am going to speculate that Odegaard is going to be offered a new contract given his status in the team and because his role is a little more holistic and he doesn’t solely operate in the final third.

Which leaves us with Havertz. I rate Havertz really highly and believe he is integral to Arsenal’s style, he has the technical quality to play one touch football and the physical quality to act as a release valve and hold the ball up. I can’t think of many forwards who offer both sides of the game to such an extent.

In a recent development, there are several Arsenal attackers I would trade in before Havertz. However, the market doesn’t always bend to your will. Arsenal remain a self sustaining club and in the PSR / SCR era, player trading has never been more key or more voluminous. Keeping money swishing between the cost and revenue columns is a necessity in this environment.

Clearly, the number one impediment to Havertz getting a new deal is his fitness. He is still clearly preferred by the manager to Viktor Gyokeres. I have to say I am surprised (a little unpleasantly) at how quickly the tide of opinion has turned against Havertz. The run he went on very recently that saw him score in the Champions League Final, score the goal that clinched the title against Burnley, a critical goal against Chelsea and the winning goal at Anfield seem to have just bought him absolutely no credit within the fan base, which I find a little surprising.

However, Arsenal need to boost their attacking prowess overall at some point very soon. Like I noted, I would consider Havertz a superior player to all of Eze, Gyokeres, Tzolis and Madueke. The squad is well served for numbers in attack; it doesn’t have any gaps in that respect. It has a gap in elite quality.

In a recent development, the key to boosting that might not be ‘who is the least effective player?’ it might be ‘who is the most saleable?’ Sometimes you do just have to cash in your chips on a player to evolve and move forwards. It doesn’t always have to be because the player is obsolete or not good enough. Arsenal have such numbers in midfield that there also isn’t really a route into the team there for Havertz either.

If someone offered £60-70m for Gyokeres or Eze, I would accept it and give Havertz a new contract the next day (assuming he does prove his fitness). But I think those scenarios are unlikely. I am not arguing that we have definitely reached the ‘we must sell Kai’ stage and I will reiterate that, at this moment in time, I consider him a very key player who should pretty much always start when fit.

While he isn’t the most prolific finisher as a centre-forward, crucial goals this season against Chelsea and Liverpool demonstrate his worth. The conversation about moving on only becomes live on condition that the money is used to immediately buy an obviously elite attacker- preferably a centre-forward in that case since that is the gap a Havertz departure would leave.

It has been revealed that but I am certain it is a conversation Arteta and Andrea Berta are at the moment entertaining. Arteta will want to push the level of the team even further and, to fund what that is going to entail, potentially painful sales will have to be made somewhere. The vigour with which the club pursued the sale of Gabriel Martinelli this summer demonstrates the manager has the stomach for that conversation too.

A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

Logic control of NeuroAxis during closed-loop glucose-responsive neuromodulation. The NeuroAxis-mediated VNS is triggered only after the glucose level exceeds a threshold of five consecutive readings. Once the stimulation condition is met, the system delivers biphasic electrical pulses for 3 min.

Some Friday stuff about things

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mikel Arteta’s press conference takes place early this morning, rather than the typical 1.30pm start time.
  • It has been revealed that so, the talking points will come later, if there are any talking points.
  • Also, the bloke from Sky Sports will come to the press conference dressed up as a PS5 controller to ask if the manager is concerned about his players staying up all night to to play Grand Theft Auto 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta’s press conference takes place early this morning, rather than the typical 1.30pm start time. I woke up a bit later than usual, and there’s part of me that wonders if I should wait for it before doing the blog, but then that would make the blog a lot later than usual and I don’t want to disrupt anybody’s routine. Especially on a Friday.

It has been revealed that so, the talking points will come later, if there are any talking points. My guesses on questions today:.

Also, the bloke from Sky Sports will come to the press conference dressed up as a PS5 controller to ask if the manager is concerned about his players staying up all night to to play Grand Theft Auto 6. Hopefully he requires a firmware revision before speaking.

It has been revealed that so, in the absence of news and stuff to talk about, I thought I’d point you in the direction of some stuff elsewhere. In a week where we’ve been handing out newly introduced contracts all over the place, Phil Costa wonders about the future of Kai Havertz and whether new terms might be on offer for him.

It’s an interesting one because I think it’s clear he’s the manager’s first preference from the two strikers he has available to him. If he was forced to drive deep into the woods and leave one tied to a tree, it’d be Viktor Gyokeres left in the dark forest to try and undo his knots and make his way back to civilisation. But reservations about Kai’s fitness are more than understandable, and while this is a player who has scored major goals for this club since his arrival, there are inconsistencies to his game that can be frustrating.

Sources indicate that he turns 28 in June, which is far from over the hill, but it’s then about the cost of a multi-year commitment to a player who, more than likely, you’re probably never going to get much of a return on. Particularly if you have to add to what is already a significant weekly wage packet, even if others will have taken over the mantle of Arsenal’s best-paid player.

Sources indicate that my gut feeling is that we’ll probably keep him though, and jokes aside it probably is connected to Gyokeres. The Swedish international feels like the player most expendable of the two in the manager’s mind, and I just can’t really see any scenario when simply Arsenal hang onto both for another season or two, or decide that both can be sold and then replaced at the same time. We sold two left-wingers and a striker this summer and replaced them with one single player, so it’s not as if our track record of augmenting the squad in forward areas would give you much confidence in our ability to undergo sweeping reform.

According to recent reports, thus, some consistency will be necessary, and if push comes to shove, Arteta will sell Gyokeres a hundred times before Havertz once – unless there’s something to do with fitness/injury. The question then is do we renew now, or see where we are next summer? If we add a younger striker to the mix, the benefit of Havertz’s experience isn’t to be underestimated, and then in those final 12 months, if there’s a deal to be done it can be done, and if not, the club have time to consider other options. At that point, he’ll be almost 29, he’ll have options elsewhere if there’s no future at Arsenal.

Of course players want some security when it comes to their contracts and their futures, it might be a case he wants that and that may force the issue one way or the other, but as it stands, it doesn’t seem to be an issue that absolutely has to be a top priority right now (unlike someone like Declan Rice, for example).

It has been revealed that for more good reading this morning, Lewis writes about Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino (the big lumpy prick), and the challenges they face with their latest clubs. I know I remarked this on the Arsecast Extra earlier in the week, but I really feel like the latter escapes the scrutiny he deserves for the evil he has perpetrated throughout his career. Manager of Sp*rs, Chelsea and PSG, and now Man Utd, as well as a stint as a national manager during which I thought he thoroughly shamed himself over the Folarin Balogun incident in the World Cup. I know he’s a big mate of Mikel Arteta, but for me he’s up there with the worst of them. A Maroon5 cover of a Phil Collins song brought to life.

Bayern Munich and England star Harry Kane has vowed to return for the "business end of the season" after undergoing ankle surgery.

The striker sustained an ankle ligament injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw against FC Koln on Friday evening.

Kane attempted to carry on after being caught in a tackle from Koln defender Joel Schmied before he received treatment and made way for Tom Bischof in the 20th minute.

Bayern released a statement after the game, revealing Kane would be out for a "few months" with a "torn syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle".

According to recent reports, in a fresh upgrade on Saturday morning, Bayern said: "Harry Kane underwent successful surgery overnight following the syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle, which he sustained in yesterday’s Bundesliga match against 1. FC Köln.

"The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program.".

Kane also shared a defiant message on social media, accompanied by an image of him sitting on a hospital bed with his left foot in a protective boot.

"The highs and lows of life!" Kane wrote. "Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

“‘Tough times don’t last, tough people do’ - my guy Julian Edelman (three-time Super Bowl winner) told me this one!

In a recent development, “Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut!”.

Industry observers note that the highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. With Kane likely to be out until the end of February, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany will have to come up with solutions to negate the impact of being without his star striker.

Ismael Saibari can play as a centre-forward, but he is currently sidelined with the same injury as Kane, putting him out of action until the start of February.

Serge Gnabry is also on the sidelines and is unlikely to be back until the turn of the year, leaving Kompany without another potential candidate to fill the void created by Kane's absence.

Noah Codjo-Evora is an option if Kompany decides to put his faith in youth, but the 19-year-old is unlikely to start regularly given the fact he only made his first-team debut as a substitute on Friday.

That means Kompany will likely opt to field a false nine in the coming weeks and months, which is a role Lennart Karl played when Kane went off against Koln.

Recent findings suggest that gleison Bremer's equaliser earned Juventus a point at the Stadio Artemio Franchi after they twice fell behind against Fiorentina. Spalletti's side now go into the international break outside the Champions League places, with their next home game brought forward by a day.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

It has been revealed that the hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

Sources indicate that the closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

In a recent development, referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Spalletti made three changes in the 57th minute, sending on Zhegrova for Woltemade, Alajbegovic for Boga and Celik for Cabal. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

Recent findings suggest that at his press conference at the Franchi, Spalletti said he was not happy because his team does not play at a steady enough level to aim for anything important. He did praise Kolo Muani, describing him as the player everyone wanted and one he can use as a centre-forward or out wide. Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.
